ityete vahnayaḥ proktāḥ praṇīyante 'dhvareṣu ca //
1.6.d:
विसृज्य सप्तकं चादौ चत्वारिंशन्नवैव च
इत्येते वह्नयः प्रोक्ताः प्रणीयन्ते ऽध्वरेषु च ॥
1.6.m: Adding forty-nine to the original group of seven, / these fires have been proclaimed; they are brought forth in sacrificial rites.

1.6.s:
sarve tapasvinastvete sarve vratabhṛtaḥ smṛtāḥ
prajānāṃ patayaḥ sarve sarve rudrātmakāḥ smṛtāḥ //
1.6.d:
सर्वे तपस्विनस्त्वेते सर्वे व्रतभृतः स्मृताः
प्रजानां पतयः सर्वे सर्वे रुद्रात्मकाः स्मृताः ॥
1.6.m: All of them are ascetics, all are remembered as holders of vows, / all are lords of creatures, and all are remembered as having the nature of Rudra.

1.6.s:
ayajvānaś ca yajvānaḥ pitaraḥ prītimānasāḥ
agniṣvāttāś ca yajvānaḥ śeṣā barhiṣadaḥ smṛtāḥ //
1.6.d:
अयज्वानश् च यज्वानः पितरः प्रीतिमानसाः
अग्निष्वात्ताश् च यज्वानः शेषा बर्हिषदः स्मृताः ॥
1.6.m: Non-sacrificers and sacrificers, the ancestors with joyful minds: / the sacrificers are the Agniṣvāttas, and the rest are remembered as Barhiṣads.

1.6.s:
menāṃ tu mānasīṃ teṣāṃ janayāmāsa vai svadhā
agniṣvāttātmajā menā mānasī lokaviśrutā //
1.6.d:
मेनां तु मानसीं तेषां जनयामास वै स्वधा
अग्निष्वात्तात्मजा मेना मानसी लोकविश्रुता ॥
1.6.m: Svadhā gave birth to Menā, the mind-born [daughter] of those [ancestors]. / Menā, the mind-born daughter of the Agniṣvāttas, is renowned throughout the world.

1.6.s:
asūta menā mainākaṃ krauñcaṃ tasyānujāmumām
gaṅgāṃ haimavatīṃ jajñe bhavāṅgāśleṣapāvanīm //
1.6.d:
असूत मेना मैनाकं क्रौञ्चं तस्यानुजामुमाम्
गङ्गां हैमवतीं जज्ञे भवाङ्गाश्लेषपावनीम् ॥
1.6.m: Menā gave birth to Maināka, Krauñca, and his younger sister Umā, / and Gaṅgā the daughter of Himavat, who purifies through the embrace of the limbs of Bhava.

1.6.s:
dharaṇīṃ janayāmāsa mānasīṃ yajñayājinīm
svadhā sā merurājasya patnī padmasamānanā //
1.6.d:
धरणीं जनयामास मानसीं यज्ञयाजिनीम्
स्वधा सा मेरुराजस्य पत्नी पद्मसमानना ॥
1.6.m:
Svadhā, the lotus-faced wife of Mount Meru the king,
bore the mind-born Dharaṇī, who performs sacrifices.

1.6.s:
pitaro 'mṛtapāḥ proktās teṣāṃ caiveha vistaraḥ
ṛṣīṇāṃ ca kulaṃ sarvaṃ śṛṇudhvaṃ tatsuvistaram //
1.6.d:
पितरो ऽमृतपाः प्रोक्तास् तेषां चैवेह विस्तरः
ऋषीणां च कुलं सर्वं शृणुध्वं तत्सुविस्तरम् ॥
1.6.m:
The ancestors are declared to be drinkers of nectar; their extent is here,
and listen in full detail to the whole lineage of the ṛṣis.

1.6.s:
vadāmi pṛthagadhyāyasaṃsthitaṃ vastadūrdhvataḥ
dākṣāyaṇī satī yātā pārśvaṃ rudrasya pārvatī //
1.6.d:
वदामि पृथगध्यायसंस्थितं वस्तदूर्ध्वतः
दाक्षायणी सती याता पार्श्वं रुद्रस्य पार्वती ॥
1.6.m:
I shall tell it to you, set down in separate chapters, from this point forward.
Satī, Dakṣa's daughter, as Pārvatī, went to Rudra's side.

1.6.s:
paścāddakṣaṃ vinindyaiṣā patiṃ lebhe bhavaṃ tathā
tāṃ dhyātvā vyasṛjadrudrān anekānnīlalohitaḥ //
1.6.d:
पश्चाद्दक्षं विनिन्द्यैषा पतिं लेभे भवं तथा
तां ध्यात्वा व्यसृजद्रुद्रान् अनेकान्नीललोहितः ॥
1.6.m:
Later, having rebuked Dakṣa, she obtained Bhava as her husband.
Meditating on her, the blue-and-red god emanated many Rudras,

1.6.s:
ātmanastu samānsarvān sarvalokanamaskṛtān
yācito muniśārdūlā brahmaṇā prahasan kṣaṇāt //
1.6.d:
आत्मनस्तु समान्सर्वान् सर्वलोकनमस्कृतान्
याचितो मुनिशार्दूला ब्रह्मणा प्रहसन् क्षणात् ॥
1.6.m:
All equal to himself and bowed to by all the worlds.
Implored by Brahmā, O tigers among sages, he laughed and instantly [created them].

1.6.s:
taistu saṃchāditaṃ sarvaṃ caturdaśavidhaṃ jagat
tāndṛṣṭvā vividhān rudrān nirmalānnīlalohitān //
1.6.d:
तैस्तु संछादितं सर्वं चतुर्दशविधं जगत्
तान्दृष्ट्वा विविधान् रुद्रान् निर्मलान्नीललोहितान् ॥
1.6.m:
By them the entire fourteenfold world was covered.
Seeing those diverse Rudras, spotless and blue-and-red,

1.6.s:
jarāmaraṇanirmuktān prāha rudrānpitāmahaḥ
namo 'stu vo mahādevās trinetrā nīlalohitāḥ //
1.6.d:
जरामरणनिर्मुक्तान् प्राह रुद्रान्पितामहः
नमो ऽस्तु वो महादेवास् त्रिनेत्रा नीललोहिताः ॥
1.6.m:
Freed from old age and death, Pitāmaha said to the Rudras:
“Obeisance to you, O Mahādevas, three-eyed and blue-and-red,

1.6.s:
sarvajñāḥ sarvagā dīrghā hrasvā vāmanakāḥ śubhāḥ
hiraṇyakeśā dṛṣṭighnā nityā buddhāś ca nirmalāḥ //
1.6.d:
सर्वज्ञाः सर्वगा दीर्घा ह्रस्वा वामनकाः शुभाः
हिरण्यकेशा दृष्टिघ्ना नित्या बुद्धाश् च निर्मलाः ॥
1.6.m:
Omniscient, omnipresent, tall, short, dwarf-like, auspicious,
Golden-haired, destroyers of [evil] gaze, eternal, enlightened, and stainless,

1.6.s:
nirdvaṃdvā vītarāgāś ca viśvātmāno bhavātmajāḥ
evaṃ stutvā tadā rudrān rudraṃ cāha bhavaṃ śivam
pradakṣiṇīkṛtya tadā bhagavānkanakāṇḍajaḥ //
1.6.d:
निर्द्वंद्वा वीतरागाश् च विश्वात्मानो भवात्मजाः
एवं स्तुत्वा तदा रुद्रान् रुद्रं चाह भवं शिवम्
प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य तदा भगवान्कनकाण्डजः ॥
1.6.m:
Free from dualities, detached from passion, the self of the universe, born from Bhava!”
Having thus praised the Rudras, the lord born from the golden egg,
having circumambulated Rudra, who is Bhava and Śiva, said:

1.6.s:
namo 'stu te mahādeva prajā nārhasi śaṃkara
mṛtyuhīnā vibho sraṣṭuṃ mṛtyuyuktāḥ sṛja prabho //
1.6.d:
नमो ऽस्तु ते महादेव प्रजा नार्हसि शंकर
मृत्युहीना विभो स्रष्टुं मृत्युयुक्ताः सृज प्रभो ॥
1.6.m:
“Obeisance to you, O Mahādeva! O Śaṅkara, you should not
create creatures devoid of death, O pervasive lord; create those subject to death, O master!”

1.6.s:
tatastamāha bhagavān na hi me tādṛśī sthitiḥ
sa tvaṃ sṛja yathākāmaṃ mṛtyuyuktāḥ prajāḥ prabho //
1.6.d:
ततस्तमाह भगवान् न हि मे तादृशी स्थितिः
स त्वं सृज यथाकामं मृत्युयुक्ताः प्रजाः प्रभो ॥
1.6.m:
Then the blessed lord said to him: “Such an arrangement is not mine.
Do you yourself create, as you wish, creatures subject to death, O master!”

1.6.s:
labdhvā sasarja sakalaṃ śaṃkarāccaturānanaḥ
jarāmaraṇasaṃyuktaṃ jagadetaccarācaram //
1.6.d:
लब्ध्वा ससर्ज सकलं शंकराच्चतुराननः
जरामरणसंयुक्तं जगदेतच्चराचरम् ॥
1.6.m:
Having received [permission] from Śaṅkara, the four-faced lord created all
this universe of the moving and unmoving, endowed with old age and death.

1.6.s:
śaṃkaro 'pi tadā rudrair nivṛttātmā hyadhiṣṭhitaḥ
sthāṇutvaṃ tasya vai viprāḥ śaṃkarasya mahātmanaḥ //
1.6.d:
शंकरो ऽपि तदा रुद्रैर् निवृत्तात्मा ह्यधिष्ठितः
स्थाणुत्वं तस्य वै विप्राः शंकरस्य महात्मनः ॥
1.6.m:
Śaṅkara too was then attended by the Rudras whose nature is turned away [from worldly action].
His state as Sthāṇu, O brāhmaṇas, belongs indeed to that great-souled Śaṅkara,

1.6.s:
niṣkalasyātmanaḥ śambhoḥ svecchādhṛtaśarīriṇaḥ
śaṃ rudraḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ karoti ghṛṇayā yataḥ //
1.6.d:
निष्कलस्यात्मनः शम्भोः स्वेच्छाधृतशरीरिणः
शं रुद्रः सर्वभूतानां करोति घृणया यतः ॥
1.6.m:
To the partless self, Sambhu, who assumes a body by his own will;
for Rudra works welfare (śaṃ) for all beings out of compassion.

1.6.s:
śaṃkaraścāprayatnena tadātmā yogavidyayā
vairāgyasthaṃ viraktasya vimuktiryacchamucyate //
1.6.d:
शंकरश्चाप्रयत्नेन तदात्मा योगविद्यया
वैराग्यस्थं विरक्तस्य विमुक्तिर्यच्छमुच्यते ॥
1.6.m:
And Śaṅkara, without effort, by the knowledge of yoga has that nature;
for one grounded in dispassion and detached, liberation is called the highest peace.

1.6.s:
aṇostu viṣayatyāgaḥ saṃsārabhayataḥ kramāt
vairāgyājjāyate puṃso virāgo darśanāntare //
1.6.d:
अणोस्तु विषयत्यागः संसारभयतः क्रमात्
वैराग्याज्जायते पुंसो विरागो दर्शनान्तरे ॥
1.6.m:
The gradual abandonment of sense-objects by the individual self out of fear of saṃsāra
arises from dispassion; in the other view, a man becomes detached

1.6.s:
vimukhyo viguṇatyāgo vijñānasyāvicārataḥ
tasya cāsya ca saṃdhānaṃ prasādātparameṣṭhinaḥ //
1.6.d:
विमुख्यो विगुणत्यागो विज्ञानस्याविचारतः
तस्य चास्य च संधानं प्रसादात्परमेष्ठिनः ॥
1.6.m:
By turning away, by abandoning the gunas, and by unquestioning wisdom;
and the union of that and of this comes about through the grace of the Supreme Lord.

1.6.s:
dharmo jñānaṃ ca vairāgyam aiśvaryaṃ śaṃkarādiha
sa eva śaṃkaraḥ sākṣāt pinākī nīlalohitaḥ //
1.6.d:
धर्मो ज्ञानं च वैराग्यम् ऐश्वर्यं शंकरादिह
स एव शंकरः साक्षात् पिनाकी नीललोहितः ॥
1.6.m:
Dharma, knowledge, dispassion, and sovereign power here [arise] from Śaṅkara.
He alone is Śaṅkara directly, the Pinākin, the blue-and-red god.

1.6.s:
ye śaṃkarāśritāḥ sarve mucyante te na saṃśayaḥ
na gacchantyeva narakaṃ pāpiṣṭhā api dāruṇam //
1.6.d:
ये शंकराश्रिताः सर्वे मुच्यन्ते ते न संशयः
न गच्छन्त्येव नरकं पापिष्ठा अपि दारुणम् ॥
1.6.m:
All those who take refuge in Śaṅkara are liberated, without doubt;
even the most wicked do not go to dreadful hell.

1.6.s:
āśritāḥ śaṃkaraṃ tasmāt prāpnuvanti ca śāśvatam
māyāntāścaiva ghorādyā hy aṣṭaviṃśatireva ca //
1.6.d:
आश्रिताः शंकरं तस्मात् प्राप्नुवन्ति च शाश्वतम्
मायान्ताश्चैव घोराद्या ह्य् अष्टविंशतिरेव च ॥
1.6.m:
Therefore, taking refuge in Śaṅkara, they reach the eternal.
Ending with Māyā, beginning with Ghora, there are indeed twenty-eight

1.6.s:
koṭayo narakāṇāṃ tu pacyante tāsu pāpinaḥ
anāśritāḥ śivaṃ rudraṃ śaṃkaraṃ nīlalohitam //
1.6.d:
कोटयो नरकाणां तु पच्यन्ते तासु पापिनः
अनाश्रिताः शिवं रुद्रं शंकरं नीललोहितम् ॥
1.6.m:
Crores of hells, and in them sinners are cooked
who have not taken refuge in Śiva, Rudra, Śaṅkara, the blue-and-red god,

1.6.s:
āśrayaṃ sarvabhūtānām avyayaṃ jagatāṃ patim
puruṣaṃ paramātmānaṃ puruhūtaṃ puruṣṭutam //
1.6.d:
आश्रयं सर्वभूतानाम् अव्ययं जगतां पतिम्
पुरुषं परमात्मानं पुरुहूतं पुरुष्टुतम् ॥
1.6.m:
The refuge of all beings, the imperishable lord of the worlds,
the Puruṣa, the Supreme Self, invoked by many, praised by many;

1.6.s:
tamasā kālarudrākhyaṃ rajasā kanakāṇḍajam
sattvena sarvagaṃ viṣṇuṃ nirguṇatve maheśvaram //
1.6.d:
तमसा कालरुद्राख्यं रजसा कनकाण्डजम्
सत्त्वेन सर्वगं विष्णुं निर्गुणत्वे महेश्वरम् ॥
1.6.m:
Through tamas named Kālarudra, through rajas the one born from the golden egg,
through sattva the all-pervading Viṣṇu, and in his attributeless nature Maheśvara.

1.6.s:
kena gacchanti narakaṃ narāḥ kena mahāmate
karmaṇākarmaṇā vāpi śrotuṃ kautūhalaṃ hi naḥ //
1.6.d:
केन गच्छन्ति नरकं नराः केन महामते
कर्मणाकर्मणा वापि श्रोतुं कौतूहलं हि नः ॥
1.6.m:
By what do men go to hell, O highly intelligent one? By what
action or inaction? We are curious to hear.

1.7.s:
sūta uvāca
rahasyaṃ vaḥ pravakṣyāmi bhavasyāmitatejasaḥ
prabhāvaṃ śaṃkarasyādyaṃ saṃkṣepātsarvadarśinaḥ //
1.7.d:
सूत उवाच
रहस्यं वः प्रवक्ष्यामि भवस्यामिततेजसः
प्रभावं शंकरस्याद्यं संक्षेपात्सर्वदर्शिनः ॥
1.7.m:
Sūta said:
I shall tell you in brief the secret of Bhava of boundless splendor,
the primal majesty of Śaṅkara, the all-seeing.

1.7.s: yoginaḥ sarvatattvajñāḥ paraṃ vairāgyamāsthitāḥ //
1.7.d: योगिनः सर्वतत्त्वज्ञाः परं वैराग्यमास्थिताः ॥
1.7.m: Yogins who know all truths and have attained supreme dispassion,

1.7.s: prāṇāyāmādibhiścāṣṭasādhanaiḥ sahacāriṇaḥ //
1.7.d: प्राणायामादिभिश्चाष्टसाधनैः सहचारिणः ॥
1.7.m: Practicing along with the eight means, beginning with breath-control,

1.7.s:
karuṇādiguṇopetāḥ kṛtvāpi vividhāni te
karmāṇi narakaṃ svargaṃ gacchantyeva svakarmaṇā //
1.7.d:
करुणादिगुणोपेताः कृत्वापि विविधानि ते
कर्माणि नरकं स्वर्गं गच्छन्त्येव स्वकर्मणा ॥
1.7.m:
Endowed with virtues like compassion—even after performing various
deeds, they go to hell or heaven solely by their own karma.

1.7.s:
prasādājjāyate jñānaṃ jñānādyogaḥ pravartate
yogena jāyate muktiḥ prasādādakhilaṃ tataḥ //
1.7.d:
प्रसादाज्जायते ज्ञानं ज्ञानाद्योगः प्रवर्तते
योगेन जायते मुक्तिः प्रसादादखिलं ततः ॥
1.7.m:
From grace knowledge is born, from knowledge yoga proceeds,
through yoga liberation arises; therefore, everything [comes] from grace.

1.7.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ
prasādād yadi vijñānaṃ svarūpaṃ vaktumarhasi
divyaṃ māheśvaraṃ caiva yogaṃ yogavidāṃ vara //
1.7.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः
प्रसादाद् यदि विज्ञानं स्वरूपं वक्तुमर्हसि
दिव्यं माहेश्वरं चैव योगं योगविदां वर ॥
1.7.m:
The sages said:
If wisdom comes from grace, you should tell us the true nature
of divine, Māheśvara yoga, O best of the knowers of yoga!

1.7.s:
kathaṃ karoti bhagavān cintayā rahitaḥ śivaḥ
prasādaṃ yogamārgeṇa kasminkāle nṛṇāṃ vibhuḥ //
1.7.d:
कथं करोति भगवान् चिन्तया रहितः शिवः
प्रसादं योगमार्गेण कस्मिन्काले नृणां विभुः ॥
1.7.m:
How does the blessed lord Śiva, free from thought,
grant grace by means of yoga, and at what time to men, O pervasive lord?

1.7.s:
romaharṣaṇa uvāca
devānāṃ ca ṛṣīṇāṃ ca pitṝṇāṃ saṃnidhau purā
śailādinā tu kathitaṃ śṛṇvantu brahmasūnave //
1.7.d:
रोमहर्षण उवाच
देवानां च ऋषीणां च पितॄणां संनिधौ पुरा
शैलादिना तु कथितं शृण्वन्तु ब्रह्मसूनवे ॥
1.7.m:
Romaharṣaṇa said:
Listen to what was told formerly to the son of Brahmā by Śailādi
in the presence of the gods, the ṛṣis, and the ancestors:

1.7.s:
vyāsāvatārāṇi tathā dvāparānte ca suvratāḥ
yogācāryāvatārāṇi tathā tiṣye tu śūlinaḥ //
1.7.d:
व्यासावताराणि तथा द्वापरान्ते च सुव्रताः
योगाचार्यावताराणि तथा तिष्ये तु शूलिनः ॥
1.7.m:
The incarnations of Vyāsa at the close of Dvāpara, O you of virtuous vows,
and the incarnations of the trident-wielding lord as masters of yoga in the Kali age;

1.7.s:
tatratatra vibhoḥ śiṣyāś catvāraḥ śamabhājanāḥ
praśiṣyā bahavasteṣāṃ prasīdatyevamīśvaraḥ //
1.7.d:
तत्रतत्र विभोः शिष्याश् चत्वारः शमभाजनाः
प्रशिष्या बहवस्तेषां प्रसीदत्येवमीश्वरः ॥
1.7.m:
In each case there are four disciples of the pervasive lord, vessels of tranquility,
and their grand-disciples are many; thus the Lord becomes gracious.

1.7.s:
evaṃ kramāgataṃ jñānaṃ mukhādeva nṛṇāṃ vibhoḥ
vaiśyāntaṃ brāhmaṇādyaṃ hi ghṛṇayā cānurūpataḥ //
1.7.d:
एवं क्रमागतं ज्ञानं मुखादेव नृणां विभोः
वैश्यान्तं ब्राह्मणाद्यं हि घृणया चानुरूपतः ॥
1.7.m:
Thus knowledge has been handed down directly from the mouth of the pervasive lord to men,
beginning with brāhmaṇas and ending with vaiśyas, out of compassion and according to suitability.

1.7.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ
dvāpare dvāpare vyāsāḥ ke vai kutrāntareṣu vai
kalpeṣu kasminkalpe no vaktumarhasi cātra tān //
1.7.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः
द्वापरे द्वापरे व्यासाः के वै कुत्रान्तरेषु वै
कल्पेषु कस्मिन्कल्पे नो वक्तुमर्हसि चात्र तान् ॥
1.7.m:
The sages said:
Who were the Vyāsas in each Dvāpara, in which intervals,
and in which kalpa among kalpas? You should tell us about them here.

1.7.s:
sūta uvāca
śṛṇvantu kalpe vārāhe dvijā vaivasvatāntare
vyāsāṃś ca sāmprataṃ rudrāṃs tathā sarvāntareṣu vai //
1.7.d:
सूत उवाच
शृण्वन्तु कल्पे वाराहे द्विजा वैवस्वतान्तरे
व्यासांश् च साम्प्रतं रुद्रांस् तथा सर्वान्तरेषु वै ॥
1.7.m:
Sūta said:
Listen, O twice-born, to the Vyāsas in the Vārāha kalpa during the Vaivasvata interval
and now to the Rudras, as well as in all the intervals,

1.7.s:
vedānāṃ ca purāṇānāṃ tathā jñānapradarśakān
yathākramaṃ pravakṣyāmi sarvāvarteṣu sāmpratam //
1.7.d:
वेदानां च पुराणानां तथा ज्ञानप्रदर्शकान्
यथाक्रमं प्रवक्ष्यामि सर्वावर्तेषु साम्प्रतम् ॥
1.7.m:
Those who reveal the Vedas and the Purāṇas, as well as knowledge;
I shall declare them now in due order throughout all the cycles.

1.7.s:
kratuḥ satyo bhārgavaś ca aṅgirāḥ savitā dvijāḥ
mṛtyuḥ śatakraturdhīmān vasiṣṭho munipuṃgavaḥ //
1.7.d:
क्रतुः सत्यो भार्गवश् च अङ्गिराः सविता द्विजाः
मृत्युः शतक्रतुर्धीमान् वसिष्ठो मुनिपुंगवः ॥
1.7.m:
Kratu, Satya, Bhārgava, Aṅgiras, Savitṛ, O twice-born,
Mṛtyu, the wise Śatakratu, Vasiṣṭha the bull among sages,

1.7.s:
sārasvatastridhāmā ca trivṛto munipuṃgavaḥ
śatatejāḥ svayaṃdharmo nārāyaṇa iti śrutaḥ //
1.7.d:
सारस्वतस्त्रिधामा च त्रिवृतो मुनिपुंगवः
शततेजाः स्वयंधर्मो नारायण इति श्रुतः ॥
1.7.m:
Sārasvata, Tridhāman, Trivṛta the bull among sages,
Śatatejas, Svayaṃdharma, and the one known as Nārāyaṇa,

1.7.s:
tarakṣuścāruṇirdhīmāṃs tathā devaḥ kṛtaṃjayaḥ
ṛtaṃjayo bharadvājo gautamaḥ kavisattamaḥ //
1.7.d:
तरक्षुश्चारुणिर्धीमांस् तथा देवः कृतंजयः
ऋतंजयो भरद्वाजो गौतमः कविसत्तमः ॥
1.7.m:
Tarakṣu, the wise Āruṇi, and Deva, Kṛtaṃjaya,
Ṛtaṃjaya, Bharadvāja, Gautama the best of poets,

1.7.s:
vācaśravā muniḥ sākṣāt tathā śuṣmāyaṇiḥ śuciḥ
tṛṇabindur munī rūkṣaḥ śaktiḥ śākteya uttaraḥ //
1.7.d:
वाचश्रवा मुनिः साक्षात् तथा शुष्मायणिः शुचिः
तृणबिन्दुर् मुनी रूक्षः शक्तिः शाक्तेय उत्तरः ॥
1.7.m:
The sage Vācaśravas in person, and the pure Śuṣmāyaṇi,
Tṛṇabindu the austere sage, Śakti, and next the son of Śakti,

1.7.s:
jātūkarṇyo hariḥ sākṣāt kṛṣṇadvaipāyano muniḥ
vyāsāstvete ca śṛṇvantu kalau yogeśvarān kramāt //
1.7.d:
जातूकर्ण्यो हरिः साक्षात् कृष्णद्वैपायनो मुनिः
व्यासास्त्वेते च शृण्वन्तु कलौ योगेश्वरान् क्रमात् ॥
1.7.m:
Jātūkarṇya, and Hari in person, the sage Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana.
These are the Vyāsas; now listen to the lords of yoga in the Kali age in order.

1.7.s:
asaṃkhyātā hi kalpeṣu vibhoḥ sarvāntareṣu ca
kalau rudrāvatārāṇāṃ vyāsānāṃ kila gauravāt //
1.7.d:
असंख्याता हि कल्पेषु विभोः सर्वान्तरेषु च
कलौ रुद्रावताराणां व्यासानां किल गौरवात् ॥
1.7.m:
Countless indeed across the kalpas and in all the intervals of the pervasive lord
are the incarnations of Rudra in Kali, out of reverence for the Vyāsas.

1.7.s:
vaivasvatāntare kalpe vārāhe ye ca tān punaḥ
avatārān pravakṣyāmi tathā sarvāntareṣu vai //
1.7.d:
वैवस्वतान्तरे कल्पे वाराहे ये च तान् पुनः
अवतारान् प्रवक्ष्यामि तथा सर्वान्तरेषु वै ॥
1.7.m:
I shall speak again of those incarnations which occur in the Vaivasvata interval
of the Vārāha kalpa, and likewise in all intervals.

1.7.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ
manvantarāṇi vārāhe vaktumarhasi sāmpratam
tathaiva cordhvakalpeṣu siddhānvaivasvatāntare //
1.7.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः
मन्वन्तराणि वाराहे वक्तुमर्हसि साम्प्रतम्
तथैव चोर्ध्वकल्पेषु सिद्धान्वैवस्वतान्तरे ॥
1.7.m:
The sages said:
You should now tell us the manvantaras in the Vārāha [kalpa],
and likewise the accomplished ones in the higher kalpas during the Vaivasvata interval.

1.7.s:
romaharṣaṇa uvāca
manuḥ svāyambhuvastvādyas tataḥ svārociṣo dvijāḥ
uttamastāmasaścaiva raivatāścākṣuṣas tathā //
1.7.d:
रोमहर्षण उवाच
मनुः स्वायम्भुवस्त्वाद्यस् ततः स्वारोचिषो द्विजाः
उत्तमस्तामसश्चैव रैवताश्चाक्षुषस् तथा ॥
1.7.m:
Romaharṣaṇa said:
Svāyambhuva is the first Manu, then Svārociṣa, O twice-born,
Uttama, Tāmasa, Raivata, and Cākṣuṣa,

1.7.s:
vaivasvataś ca sāvarṇir dharmaḥ sāvarṇikaḥ punaḥ
piśaṅgaścāpiśaṅgābhaḥ śabalo varṇakas tathā //
1.7.d:
वैवस्वतश् च सावर्णिर् धर्मः सावर्णिकः पुनः
पिशङ्गश्चापिशङ्गाभः शबलो वर्णकस् तथा ॥
1.7.m:
Vaivasvata, Sāvarṇi, Dharma, and then Sāvarṇika,
Piśaṅga, Apiśaṅgābha, Śabala, and Varṇaka.

1.7.s:
aukārāntā akārādyā manavaḥ parikīrtitāḥ
śvetaḥ pāṇḍus tathā raktas tāmraḥ pītaśca kāpilaḥ //
1.7.d:
औकारान्ता अकाराद्या मनवः परिकीर्तिताः
श्वेतः पाण्डुस् तथा रक्तस् ताम्रः पीतश्च कापिलः ॥
1.7.m: Ending with 'au' and beginning with 'a', the Manus have been declared: / white, pale, red, copper-coloured, yellow, tawny,

1.7.s:
kṛṣṇaḥ śyāmas tathā dhūmraḥ sudhūmraś ca dvijottamāḥ
apiśaṅgaḥ piśaṅgaś ca trivarṇaḥ śabalas tathā //
1.7.d:
कृष्णः श्यामस् तथा धूम्रः सुधूम्रश् च द्विजोत्तमाः
अपिशङ्गः पिशङ्गश् च त्रिवर्णः शबलस् तथा ॥
1.7.m: black, dark, smoky, and deep smoky, O best of the twice-born; / yellowish, reddish-yellow, tricoloured, and variegated,

1.7.s:
kālaṃdhurastu kathitā varṇato manavaḥ śubhāḥ
nāmato varṇataścaiva varṇataḥ punareva ca //
1.7.d:
कालंधुरस्तु कथिता वर्णतो मनवः शुभाः
नामतो वर्णतश्चैव वर्णतः पुनरेव च ॥
1.7.m: and Kālamdhura—thus the auspicious Manus are described by their colours; / by their names, by their colours, and again by their colours.

1.7.s:
svarātmānaḥ samākhyātāś cāntareśāḥ samāsataḥ
vaivasvata ṛkārastu manuḥ kṛṣṇaḥ sureśvaraḥ //
1.7.d:
स्वरात्मानः समाख्याताश् चान्तरेशाः समासतः
वैवस्वत ऋकारस्तु मनुः कृष्णः सुरेश्वरः ॥
1.7.m: Embodying the vowels, the lords of the manvantaras have been proclaimed in brief. / Vaivasvata Manu, however, is the vowel 'ṛ', black, and the lord of the gods.

1.7.s:
saptamastasya vakṣyāmi yugāvarteṣu yoginaḥ
samatīteṣu kalpeṣu tathā cānāgateṣu vai //
1.7.d:
सप्तमस्तस्य वक्ष्यामि युगावर्तेषु योगिनः
समतीतेषु कल्पेषु तथा चानागतेषु वै ॥
1.7.m: He is the seventh; I shall speak of the yogins in his yuga-cycles, / in the past kalpas and likewise in the future ones.

1.7.s:
vārāhaḥ sāmprataṃ jñeyaḥ saptamāntarataḥ kramāt
yogāvatārāṃś ca vibhoḥ śiṣyāṇāṃ saṃtatis tathā //
1.7.d:
वाराहः साम्प्रतं ज्ञेयः सप्तमान्तरतः क्रमात्
योगावतारांश् च विभोः शिष्याणां संततिस् तथा ॥
1.7.m: The present kalpa should be known as the Vārāha, through the sequence of the seventh manvantara, / along with the yoga-incarnations of the Lord and the succession of their disciples,

1.7.s:
samprekṣya sarvakāleṣu tathāvarteṣu yoginām
ādye śvetaḥ kalau rudraḥ sutāro madanas tathā //
1.7.d:
सम्प्रेक्ष्य सर्वकालेषु तथावर्तेषु योगिनाम्
आद्ये श्वेतः कलौ रुद्रः सुतारो मदनस् तथा ॥
1.7.m: having observed them in all times and in the cycles of the yogins. / In the first Kali [yuga], Rudra was Śveta, then Sutāra and Madana,

1.7.s:
suhotraḥ kaṅkaṇaścaiva lokākṣir munisattamāḥ
jaigīṣavyo mahātejā bhagavān dadhivāhanaḥ //
1.7.d:
सुहोत्रः कङ्कणश्चैव लोकाक्षिर् मुनिसत्तमाः
जैगीषव्यो महातेजा भगवान् दधिवाहनः ॥
1.7.m: Suhotra, Kaṅkaṇa, Lokākṣi, O best of sages, / the glorious Jaigīṣavya, and the venerable Dadhivāhana,

1.7.s:
ṛṣabhaś ca munirdhīmān ugraścātriḥ subālakaḥ
gautamaścātha bhagavān sarvadevanamaskṛtaḥ //
1.7.d:
ऋषभश् च मुनिर्धीमान् उग्रश्चात्रिः सुबालकः
गौतमश्चाथ भगवान् सर्वदेवनमस्कृतः ॥
1.7.m: the wise sage Ṛṣabha, Ugra, Atri, Subālaka, / and the venerable Gautama, worshipped by all the gods,

1.7.s:
vedaśīrṣaś ca gokarṇo guhāvāsī śikhaṇḍabhṛt
jaṭāmālyaṭṭahāsaś ca dāruko lāṅgalī tathā //
1.7.d:
वेदशीर्षश् च गोकर्णो गुहावासी शिखण्डभृत्
जटामाल्यट्टहासश् च दारुको लाङ्गली तथा ॥
1.7.m: Vedaśīrṣa, Gokarṇa, Guhāvāsin, Śikhaṇḍabhṛt, / Jaṭāmālin, Aṭṭahāsa, Dāruka, and Lāṅgalin,

1.7.s:
mahākāyamuniḥ śūlī daṇḍī muṇḍīśvaraḥ svayam
sahiṣṇuḥ somaśarmā ca nakulīśo jagadguruḥ //
1.7.d:
महाकायमुनिः शूली दण्डी मुण्डीश्वरः स्वयम्
सहिष्णुः सोमशर्मा च नकुलीशो जगद्गुरुः ॥
1.7.m: the sage Mahākāya, Śūlin, Daṇḍin, Muṇḍīśvara himself, / Sahiṣṇu, Somaśarman, and Nakulīśa, the teacher of the world.

1.7.s:
vaivasvate 'ntare samyak proktā hi paramātmanaḥ
yogācāryāvatārā ye sarvāvarteṣu suvratāḥ //
1.7.d:
वैवस्वते ऽन्तरे सम्यक् प्रोक्ता हि परमात्मनः
योगाचार्यावतारा ये सर्वावर्तेषु सुव्रताः ॥
1.7.m: These have indeed been properly proclaimed as the incarnations of the Supreme Self as teachers of yoga / in all cycles during the Vaivasvata manvantara, O men of good vows.

1.7.s:
vyāsāścaivaṃ muniśreṣṭhā dvāpare dvāpare tvime
yogeśvarāṇāṃ catvāraḥ śiṣyāḥ pratyekamavyayāḥ //
1.7.d:
व्यासाश्चैवं मुनिश्रेष्ठा द्वापरे द्वापरे त्विमे
योगेश्वराणां चत्वारः शिष्याः प्रत्येकमव्ययाः ॥
1.7.m: And in the same way, O best of sages, these Vyāsas appear in each Dvāpara [yuga]. / Each of these masters of yoga has four imperishable disciples:

1.7.s:
śvetaḥ śvetaśikhaṇḍī ca śvetāśvaḥ śvetalohitaḥ
dundubhiḥ śatarūpaś ca ṛcīkaḥ ketumāṃs tathā //
1.7.d:
श्वेतः श्वेतशिखण्डी च श्वेताश्वः श्वेतलोहितः
दुन्दुभिः शतरूपश् च ऋचीकः केतुमांस् तथा ॥
1.7.m: Śveta, Śvetaśikhaṇḍin, Śvetāśva, and Śvetalohita; / Dundubhi, Śatarūpa, Ṛcīka, and Ketumant;

1.7.s:
viśokaśca vikeśaś ca vipāśaḥ pāpanāśanaḥ
sumukho durmukhaścaiva durdamo duratikramaḥ //
1.7.d:
विशोकश्च विकेशश् च विपाशः पापनाशनः
सुमुखो दुर्मुखश्चैव दुर्दमो दुरतिक्रमः ॥
1.7.m: Viśoka, Vikeśa, Vipāśa, and Pāpanāśana; / Sumukha, Durmukha, Durdama, and Duratikrama;

1.7.s:
sanakaś ca sanandaś ca prabhuryaś ca sanātanaḥ
ṛbhuḥ sanatkumāraś ca sudhāmā virajās tathā //
1.7.d:
सनकश् च सनन्दश् च प्रभुर्यश् च सनातनः
ऋभुः सनत्कुमारश् च सुधामा विरजास् तथा ॥
1.7.m: Sanaka, Sananda, and the lord Sanātana; / Ṛbhu, Sanatkumāra, Sudhāman, and Virajas;

1.7.s:
śaṅkhapād vairajaścaiva meghaḥ sārasvatas tathā
suvāhano muniśreṣṭho meghavāho mahādyutiḥ //
1.7.d:
शङ्खपाद् वैरजश्चैव मेघः सारस्वतस् तथा
सुवाहनो मुनिश्रेष्ठो मेघवाहो महाद्युतिः ॥
1.7.m: Śaṅkhapād, Vairaja, Megha, and Sārasvata; / Suvāhana, best of sages, and Meghavāha of great radiance;

1.7.s:
kapilaścāsuriścaiva tathā pañcaśikho muniḥ
vālkalaś ca mahāyogī dharmātmāno mahaujasaḥ //
1.7.d:
कपिलश्चासुरिश्चैव तथा पञ्चशिखो मुनिः
वाल्कलश् च महायोगी धर्मात्मानो महौजसः ॥
1.7.m: Kapila, Āsuri, and the sage Pañcaśikha; / and Vālkala, the great yogin—righteous souls of great energy;

1.7.s:
parāśaraś ca gargaś ca bhārgavaścāṅgirās tathā
balabandhur nirāmitraḥ ketuśṛṅgastapodhanaḥ //
1.7.d:
पराशरश् च गर्गश् च भार्गवश्चाङ्गिरास् तथा
बलबन्धुर् निरामित्रः केतुशृङ्गस्तपोधनः ॥
1.7.m: Parāśara, Garga, Bhārgava, and Aṅgiras; / Balabandhu, Nirāmitra, and Ketuśṛṅga, rich in asceticism;

1.7.s:
lambodaraś ca lambaśca lambākṣo lambakeśakaḥ
sarvajñaḥ samabuddhiś ca sādhyaḥ sarvastathaiva ca //
1.7.d:
लम्बोदरश् च लम्बश्च लम्बाक्षो लम्बकेशकः
सर्वज्ञः समबुद्धिश् च साध्यः सर्वस्तथैव च ॥
1.7.m: Lambodara, Lamba, Lambākṣa, and Lambakeśaka; / Sarvajña, Samabuddhi, Sādhya, and Sarva;

1.7.s:
sudhāmā kāśyapaścaiva vāsiṣṭho virajās tathā
atrir devasadaścaiva śravaṇo 'tha śraviṣṭhakaḥ
kuṇiś ca kuṇibāhuś ca kuśarīraḥ kunetrakaḥ //
1.7.d:
सुधामा काश्यपश्चैव वासिष्ठो विरजास् तथा
अत्रिर् देवसदश्चैव श्रवणो ऽथ श्रविष्ठकः
कुणिश् च कुणिबाहुश् च कुशरीरः कुनेत्रकः ॥
1.7.m: Sudhāman, Kāśyapa, Vāsiṣṭha, and Virajas; / Atri, Devasadas, Śravaṇa, and Śraviṣṭhaka; / Kuṇi, Kuṇibāhu, Kuśarīra, and Kunetraka;

1.7.s:
kaśyapo 'pyuśanāścaiva cyavano 'tha bṛhaspatiḥ
utathyo vāmadevaś ca mahāyogo mahābalaḥ //
1.7.d:
कश्यपो ऽप्युशनाश्चैव च्यवनो ऽथ बृहस्पतिः
उतथ्यो वामदेवश् च महायोगो महाबलः ॥
1.7.m: Kaśyapa, Uśanas, Cyavana, and Bṛhaspati; / Utathya, Vāmadeva, Mahāyoga, and Mahābala;

1.7.s:
vācaśravāḥ sudhīkaśca śyāvāśvaś ca yatīśvaraḥ
hiraṇyanābhaḥ kauśalyo logākṣiḥ kuthumis tathā //
1.7.d:
वाचश्रवाः सुधीकश्च श्यावाश्वश् च यतीश्वरः
हिरण्यनाभः कौशल्यो लोगाक्षिः कुथुमिस् तथा ॥
1.7.m: Vācaśravas, Sudhīka, and Śyāvāśva, lord of ascetics; / Hiraṇyanābha, Kauśalya, Logākṣi, and Kuthumi;

1.7.s:
sumanturbarbarī vidvān kabandhaḥ kuśikaṃdharaḥ
plakṣo dālbhyāyaṇiścaiva ketumān gopanas tathā //
1.7.d:
सुमन्तुर्बर्बरी विद्वान् कबन्धः कुशिकंधरः
प्लक्षो दाल्भ्यायणिश्चैव केतुमान् गोपनस् तथा ॥
1.7.m: Sumantu, the learned Barbarin, Kabandha, and Kuśikaṃdhara; / Plakṣa, Dālbhyāyaṇi, Ketumant, and Gopana;

1.7.s:
bhallāvī madhupiṅgaśca śvetaketustaponidhiḥ
uśiko bṛhadaśvaś ca devalaḥ kavireva ca //
1.7.d:
भल्लावी मधुपिङ्गश्च श्वेतकेतुस्तपोनिधिः
उशिको बृहदश्वश् च देवलः कविरेव च ॥
1.7.m: Bhallāvin, Madhupiṅga, and Śvetaketu, a treasure of asceticism; / Uśika, Bṛhadaśva, Devala, and Kavi;

1.7.s:
śālihotro 'gniveśaśca yuvanāśvaḥ śaradvasuḥ
chagalaḥ kuṇḍakarṇaś ca kumbhaścaiva pravāhakaḥ //
1.7.d:
शालिहोत्रो ऽग्निवेशश्च युवनाश्वः शरद्वसुः
छगलः कुण्डकर्णश् च कुम्भश्चैव प्रवाहकः ॥
1.7.m: Śālihotra, Agniveśa, Yuvanāśva, and Śaradvasu; / Chagala, Kuṇḍakarṇa, Kumbha, and Pravāhaka;

1.7.s:
ulūko vidyutaścaiva maṇḍūko hyāśvalāyanaḥ
akṣapādaḥ kumāraś ca ulūko vatsa eva ca //
1.7.d:
उलूको विद्युतश्चैव मण्डूको ह्याश्वलायनः
अक्षपादः कुमारश् च उलूको वत्स एव च ॥
1.7.m: Ulūka, Vidyuta, Maṇḍūka, and Āśvalāyana; / Akṣapāda, Kumāra, Ulūka, and Vatsa;

1.7.s:
kuśikaścaiva garbhaś ca mitraḥ kauruṣya eva ca
śiṣyāstvete mahātmānaḥ sarvāvarteṣu yoginām //
1.7.d:
कुशिकश्चैव गर्भश् च मित्रः कौरुष्य एव च
शिष्यास्त्वेते महात्मानः सर्वावर्तेषु योगिनाम् ॥
1.7.m: Kuśika, Garbha, Mitra, and Kauruṣya. / These great-souled men are the disciples of the yogins in all the cycles.

1.7.s:
vimalā brahmabhūyiṣṭhā jñānayogaparāyaṇāḥ
ete pāśupatāḥ siddhā bhasmoddhūlitavigrahāḥ //
1.7.d:
विमला ब्रह्मभूयिष्ठा ज्ञानयोगपरायणाः
एते पाशुपताः सिद्धा भस्मोद्धूलितविग्रहाः ॥
1.7.m: Pure, established in Brahman, devoted to the yoga of knowledge, / these are perfected Pāśupatas whose bodies are smeared with sacred ash.

1.7.s:
śiṣyāḥ praśiṣyāścaiteṣāṃ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
prāpya pāśupataṃ yogaṃ rudralokāya saṃsthitāḥ //
1.7.d:
शिष्याः प्रशिष्याश्चैतेषां शतशो ऽथ सहस्रशः
प्राप्य पाशुपतं योगं रुद्रलोकाय संस्थिताः ॥
1.7.m: Their disciples and disciples' disciples, in hundreds and in thousands, / having attained Pāśupata yoga, have gone to Rudra's realm.

1.7.s:
devādayaḥ piśācāntāḥ paśavaḥ parikīrtitāḥ
teṣāṃ patitvātsarveśo bhavaḥ paśupatiḥ smṛtaḥ //
1.7.d:
देवादयः पिशाचान्ताः पशवः परिकीर्तिताः
तेषां पतित्वात्सर्वेशो भवः पशुपतिः स्मृतः ॥
1.7.m: All beings from the gods down to piśācas are declared to be cattle (paśu). / Because he is their master, the Lord of all, Bhava, is remembered as Paśupati.

1.7.s:
tena praṇīto rudreṇa paśūnāṃ patinā dvijāḥ
yogaḥ pāśupato jñeyaḥ parāvaravibhūtaye //
1.7.d:
तेन प्रणीतो रुद्रेण पशूनां पतिना द्विजाः
योगः पाशुपतो ज्ञेयः परावरविभूतये ॥
1.7.m: By him, Rudra, the lord of the cattle, O twice-born, / Pāśupata yoga was taught for the sake of the highest and lowest attainments.

1.8.s:
sūta uvāca
saṃkṣepataḥ pravakṣyāmi yogasthānāni sāmpratam
kalpitāni śivenaiva hitāya jagatāṃ dvijāḥ //
1.8.d:
सूत उवाच
संक्षेपतः प्रवक्ष्यामि योगस्थानानि साम्प्रतम्
कल्पितानि शिवेनैव हिताय जगतां द्विजाः ॥
1.8.m: Sūta said: / I shall now speak in brief of the bodily centres for yoga, / appointed by Śiva himself for the welfare of the worlds, O twice-born.

1.8.s:
galādadho vitastyā yan nābherupari cottamam
yogasthānamadho nābher āvartaṃ madhyamaṃ bhruvoḥ //
1.8.d:
गलादधो वितस्त्या यन् नाभेरुपरि चोत्तमम्
योगस्थानमधो नाभेर् आवर्तं मध्यमं भ्रुवोः ॥
1.8.m: A span below the throat and above the navel is the best / centre for yoga; the intermediate one is below the navel, or the whirl between the eyebrows.

1.8.s:
sarvārthajñānaniṣpattir ātmano yoga ucyate
ekāgratā bhaveccaiva sarvadā tatprasādataḥ //
1.8.d:
सर्वार्थज्ञाननिष्पत्तिर् आत्मनो योग उच्यते
एकाग्रता भवेच्चैव सर्वदा तत्प्रसादतः ॥
1.8.m: Yoga is said to be the accomplishment of knowledge of all things for the Self. / And one-pointedness arises at all times through his grace.

1.8.s:
prasādasya svarūpaṃ yat svasaṃvedyaṃ dvijottamāḥ
vaktuṃ na śakyaṃ brahmādyaiḥ kramaśo jāyate nṛṇām //
1.8.d:
प्रसादस्य स्वरूपं यत् स्वसंवेद्यं द्विजोत्तमाः
वक्तुं न शक्यं ब्रह्माद्यैः क्रमशो जायते नृणाम् ॥
1.8.m: The nature of that grace is to be experienced only by oneself, O best of the twice-born; / it cannot be described even by Brahmā and the rest, and it arises gradually for mortals.

1.8.s:
yogaśabdena nirvāṇaṃ māheśaṃ padamucyate
tasya heturṛṣerjñānaṃ jñānaṃ tasya prasādataḥ //
1.8.d:
योगशब्देन निर्वाणं माहेशं पदमुच्यते
तस्य हेतुरृषेर्ज्ञानं ज्ञानं तस्य प्रसादतः ॥
1.8.m: By the word 'yoga', the state of nirvāṇa pertaining to Maheśvara is denoted. / The cause of that is the knowledge of the sage, and knowledge arises from his grace.

1.8.s:
jñānena nirdahetpāpaṃ nirudhya viṣayān sadā
niruddhendriyavṛttestu yogasiddhirbhaviṣyati //
1.8.d:
ज्ञानेन निर्दहेत्पापं निरुध्य विषयान् सदा
निरुद्धेन्द्रियवृत्तेस्तु योगसिद्धिर्भविष्यति ॥
1.8.m: By knowledge one should burn away sin, constantly restraining the sense-objects. / For one whose sense activities are restrained, success in yoga will arise.

1.8.s:
yogo nirodho vṛtteṣu cittasya dvijasattamāḥ
sādhanānyaṣṭadhā cāsya kathitānīha siddhaye //
1.8.d:
योगो निरोधो वृत्तेषु चित्तस्य द्विजसत्तमाः
साधनान्यष्टधा चास्य कथितानीह सिद्धये ॥
1.8.m: Yoga is the cessation of the modifications of the mind, O best of the twice-born. / And eight means are taught here for its attainment:

1.8.s:
yamastu prathamaḥ prokto dvitīyo niyamas tathā
tṛtīyamāsanaṃ proktaṃ prāṇāyāmastataḥ param //
1.8.d:
यमस्तु प्रथमः प्रोक्तो द्वितीयो नियमस् तथा
तृतीयमासनं प्रोक्तं प्राणायामस्ततः परम् ॥
1.8.m: Yama is taught as the first, and niyama as the second; / posture (āsana) is declared the third, and breath control (prāṇāyāma) after that;

1.8.s:
pratyāhāraṃ pañcamo vai dhāraṇā ca tataḥ parā
dhyānaṃ saptamamityuktaṃ samādhistvaṣṭamaḥ smṛtaḥ //
1.8.d:
प्रत्याहारं पञ्चमो वै धारणा च ततः परा
ध्यानं सप्तममित्युक्तं समाधिस्त्वष्टमः स्मृतः ॥
1.8.m: sensory withdrawal (pratyāhāra) is the fifth, and concentration (dhāraṇā) after that; / meditation (dhyāna) is said to be the seventh, and absorption (samādhi) is remembered as the eighth.

1.8.s:
tapasyuparamaścaiva yama ityabhidhīyate
ahiṃsā prathamo hetur yamasya yamināṃ varāḥ //
1.8.d:
तपस्युपरमश्चैव यम इत्यभिधीयते
अहिंसा प्रथमो हेतुर् यमस्य यमिनां वराः ॥
1.8.m: Asceticism and cessation are designated as yama. / Non-violence (ahiṃsā) is the primary root of yama, O best of the self-restrained.

1.8.s:
satyamasteyamaparaṃ brahmacaryāparigrahau
niyamasyāpi vai mūlaṃ yama eva na saṃśayaḥ //
1.8.d:
सत्यमस्तेयमपरं ब्रह्मचर्यापरिग्रहौ
नियमस्यापि वै मूलं यम एव न संशयः ॥
1.8.m: Truthfulness (satya), non-stealing (asteya), celibacy (brahmacarya), and non-possessiveness (aparigraha) are the others. / Yama is undoubtedly the root of niyama as well.

1.8.s:
ātmavat sarvabhūtānāṃ hitāyaiva pravartanam
ahiṃsaiṣā samākhyātā yā cātmajñānasiddhidā //
1.8.d:
आत्मवत् सर्वभूतानां हितायैव प्रवर्तनम्
अहिंसैषा समाख्याता या चात्मज्ञानसिद्धिदा ॥
1.8.m: Acting solely for the welfare of all beings as if for oneself— / this is declared to be non-violence, which grants the attainment of knowledge of the Self.

1.8.s:
dṛṣṭaṃ śrutaṃ cānumitaṃ svānubhūtaṃ yathārthataḥ
kathanaṃ satyamityuktaṃ parapīḍāvivarjitam //
1.8.d:
दृष्टं श्रुतं चानुमितं स्वानुभूतं यथार्थतः
कथनं सत्यमित्युक्तं परपीडाविवर्जितम् ॥
1.8.m: Speaking accurately of what is seen, heard, inferred, or personally experienced, / devoid of causing injury to others, is called truthfulness.

1.8.s:
nāślīlaṃ kīrtayedevaṃ brāhmaṇānāmiti śrutiḥ
paradoṣān parijñāya na vadediti cāparam //
1.8.d:
नाश्लीलं कीर्तयेदेवं ब्राह्मणानामिति श्रुतिः
परदोषान् परिज्ञाय न वदेदिति चापरम् ॥
1.8.m: 'One should not utter vulgarity,' thus runs the Vedic text for brahmins; / and furthermore, 'Knowing the faults of others, one should not speak of them.'

1.8.s:
anādānaṃ parasvānām āpadyapi vicārataḥ
manasā karmaṇā vācā tadasteyaṃ samāsataḥ //
1.8.d:
अनादानं परस्वानाम् आपद्यपि विचारतः
मनसा कर्मणा वाचा तदस्तेयं समासतः ॥
1.8.m: Not taking another's property through reflection, even in calamity, / in thought, word, or deed—that, in brief, is non-stealing.

1.8.s:
maithunasyāpravṛttirhi manovākkāyakarmaṇā
brahmacaryamiti proktaṃ yatīnāṃ brahmacāriṇām //
1.8.d:
मैथुनस्याप्रवृत्तिर्हि मनोवाक्कायकर्मणा
ब्रह्मचर्यमिति प्रोक्तं यतीनां ब्रह्मचारिणाम् ॥
1.8.m: Non-engagement in sexual union in action through mind, speech, or body / is proclaimed as celibacy for ascetics and religious students.

1.8.s:
iha vaikhānasānāṃ ca vidārāṇāṃ viśeṣataḥ
sadārāṇāṃ gṛhasthānaṃ tathaiva ca vadāmi vaḥ //
1.8.d:
इह वैखानसानां च विदाराणां विशेषतः
सदाराणां गृहस्थानं तथैव च वदामि वः ॥
1.8.m: Here, I also declare to you [the rule] especially for hermits, for wifeless men, / and likewise for householders with their wives.

1.8.s:
svadāre vidhivatkṛtvā nivṛttiścānyataḥ sadā
manasā karmaṇā vācā brahmacaryamiti smṛtam //
1.8.d:
स्वदारे विधिवत्कृत्वा निवृत्तिश्चान्यतः सदा
मनसा कर्मणा वाचा ब्रह्मचर्यमिति स्मृतम् ॥
1.8.m: Approaching one's own wife according to rule, and total restraint from others / in thought, action, and speech, is remembered as celibacy.

1.8.s:
medhyā svanārī sambhogaṃ kṛtvā snānaṃ samācaret
evaṃ gṛhastho yuktātmā brahmacārī na saṃśayaḥ //
1.8.d:
मेध्या स्वनारी सम्भोगं कृत्वा स्नानं समाचरेत्
एवं गृहस्थो युक्तात्मा ब्रह्मचारी न संशयः ॥
1.8.m: One's own wife is pure; having enjoyed [her], he should take a bath. / In this way the self-controlled householder is a celibate, without a doubt.

1.8.s:
ahiṃsāpyevamevaiṣā dvijagurvagnipūjane
vidhinā yādṛśī hiṃsā sā tvahiṃsā iti smṛtā //
1.8.d:
अहिंसाप्येवमेवैषा द्विजगुर्वग्निपूजने
विधिना यादृशी हिंसा सा त्वहिंसा इति स्मृता ॥
1.8.m: Non-violence is also just like this: in the worship of twice-born, guru, and fire, / whatever violence is [done] according to rule is remembered as non-violence.

1.8.s:
striyaḥ sadā parityājyāḥ saṅgaṃ naiva ca kārayet
kuṇapeṣu yathā cittaṃ tathā kuryādvicakṣaṇaḥ //
1.8.d:
स्त्रियः सदा परित्याज्याः सङ्गं नैव च कारयेत्
कुणपेषु यथा चित्तं तथा कुर्याद्विचक्षणः ॥
1.8.m: Women should always be renounced; one must not associate [with them]. / As the mind [views] corpses, so should the wise man treat [them].

1.8.s:
viṇmūtrotsargakāleṣu bahirbhūmau yathā matiḥ
tathā kāryā ratau cāpi svadāre cānyataḥ kutaḥ //
1.8.d:
विण्मूत्रोत्सर्गकालेषु बहिर्भूमौ यथा मतिः
तथा कार्या रतौ चापि स्वदारे चान्यतः कुतः ॥
1.8.m: Just as the mind is [turned] to the outer ground at times of discharging feces and urine, / so must it be done even in pleasure with one's own wife; how much more with another?

1.8.s:
aṅgārasadṛśī nārī ghṛtakumbhasamaḥ pumān
tasmānnārīṣu saṃsargaṃ dūrataḥ parivarjayet //
1.8.d:
अङ्गारसदृशी नारी घृतकुम्भसमः पुमान्
तस्मान्नारीषु संसर्गं दूरतः परिवर्जयेत् ॥
1.8.m: A woman is like a glowing charcoal, a man is like a jar of clarified butter; / therefore, one should avoid from afar contact with women.

1.8.s:
bhogena tṛptirnaivāsti viṣayāṇāṃ vicārataḥ
tasmādvirāgaḥ kartavyo manasā karmaṇā girā //
1.8.d:
भोगेन तृप्तिर्नैवास्ति विषयाणां विचारतः
तस्माद्विरागः कर्तव्यो मनसा कर्मणा गिरा ॥
1.8.m: When examined, there is never satisfaction of sense objects through enjoyment; / therefore, detachment must be cultivated in thought, action, and speech.

1.8.s:
na jātu kāmaḥ kāmānām upabhogena śāmyati
haviṣā kṛṣṇavartmeva bhūya evābhivardhate //
1.8.d:
न जातु कामः कामानाम् उपभोगेन शाम्यति
हविषा कृष्णवर्त्मेव भूय एवाभिवर्धते ॥
1.8.m: Never does desire cease by the consumption of desired objects; / like a fire with clarified butter, it only grows all the more.

1.8.s:
tasmāttyāgaḥ sadā kāryas tv amṛtatvāya yoginā
avirakto yato martyo nānāyoniṣu vartate //
1.8.d:
तस्मात्त्यागः सदा कार्यस् त्व् अमृतत्वाय योगिना
अविरक्तो यतो मर्त्यो नानायोनिषु वर्तते ॥
1.8.m: Therefore, renunciation must always be practiced by the yogin for the sake of immortality, / since an unattached mortal wanders in various wombs.

1.8.s:
tyāgenaivāmṛtatvaṃ hi śrutismṛtividāṃ varāḥ
karmaṇā prajayā nāsti dravyeṇa dvijasattamāḥ //
1.8.d:
त्यागेनैवामृतत्वं हि श्रुतिस्मृतिविदां वराः
कर्मणा प्रजया नास्ति द्रव्येण द्विजसत्तमाः ॥
1.8.m: For immortality comes only through renunciation, O best of knowers of Śruti and Smṛti; / it does not come through action, through offspring, or through wealth, O best of the twice-born.

1.8.s:
tasmādvirāgaḥ kartavyo manovākkāyakarmaṇā
ṛtau ṛtau nivṛttistu brahmacaryamiti smṛtam //
1.8.d:
तस्माद्विरागः कर्तव्यो मनोवाक्कायकर्मणा
ऋतौ ऋतौ निवृत्तिस्तु ब्रह्मचर्यमिति स्मृतम् ॥
1.8.m: Therefore, detachment must be cultivated through thought, speech, and bodily action. / Cessation [of intimacy] except in the fertile season is remembered as celibacy.

1.8.s:
yamāḥ saṃkṣepataḥ proktā niyamāṃś ca vadāmi vaḥ
śaucamijyā tapo dānaṃ svādhyāyopasthanigrahaḥ //
1.8.d:
यमाः संक्षेपतः प्रोक्ता नियमांश् च वदामि वः
शौचमिज्या तपो दानं स्वाध्यायोपस्थनिग्रहः ॥
1.8.m: The restraints have been stated in brief, and I shall tell you the observances: / purity, sacrifice, asceticism, giving, self-study, restraint of the sexual organ,

1.8.s:
vratopavāsamaunaṃ ca snānaṃ ca niyamā daśa
niyamaḥ syādanīhā ca śaucaṃ tuṣṭistapas tathā //
1.8.d:
व्रतोपवासमौनं च स्नानं च नियमा दश
नियमः स्यादनीहा च शौचं तुष्टिस्तपस् तथा ॥
1.8.m: vows, fasting, silence, and bathing are the ten observances. / The observance would be freedom from longing, purity, contentment, asceticism,

1.8.s:
japaḥ śivapraṇīdhānaṃ padmakādyaṃ tathāsanam
bāhyamābhyantaraṃ proktaṃ śaucamābhyantaraṃ varam //
1.8.d:
जपः शिवप्रणीधानं पद्मकाद्यं तथासनम्
बाह्यमाभ्यन्तरं प्रोक्तं शौचमाभ्यन्तरं वरम् ॥
1.8.m: repetition [of mantra], devotion to Śiva, and postures such as the lotus posture. / Purity is declared to be external and internal; internal is superior.

1.8.s:
bāhyaśaucena yuktaḥ saṃs tathā cābhyantaraṃ caret
āgneyaṃ vāruṇaṃ brāhmaṃ kartavyaṃ śivapūjakaiḥ //
1.8.d:
बाह्यशौचेन युक्तः संस् तथा चाभ्यन्तरं चरेत्
आग्नेयं वारुणं ब्राह्मं कर्तव्यं शिवपूजकैः ॥
1.8.m: Endowed with external purity, one should then practice internal [purity]. / Purity by fire, by water, and by prayer must be performed by worshippers of Śiva.

1.8.s:
snānaṃ vidhānataḥ samyak paścād ābhyantaraṃ caret
ā dehāntaṃ mṛdālipya tīrthatoyeṣu sarvadā //
1.8.d:
स्नानं विधानतः सम्यक् पश्चाद् आभ्यन्तरं चरेत्
आ देहान्तं मृदालिप्य तीर्थतोयेषु सर्वदा ॥
1.8.m: Having duly bathed properly, one should afterwards practice internal [purity]. / Anointing oneself with clay up to the ends of the body, always in sacred waters,

1.8.s:
avagāhyāpi malino hy antaḥ śaucavivarjitaḥ
śaivalā jhaṣakā matsyāḥ sattvā matsyopajīvinaḥ //
1.8.d:
अवगाह्यापि मलिनो ह्य् अन्तः शौचविवर्जितः
शैवला झषका मत्स्याः सत्त्वा मत्स्योपजीविनः ॥
1.8.m: even one who plunges is still soiled if destitute of internal purity. / Do moss, small fish, fish, and creatures that live on fish,

1.8.s:
sadāvagāhya salile viśuddhāḥ kiṃ dvijottamāḥ
tasmādābhyantaraṃ śaucaṃ sadā kāryaṃ vidhānataḥ //
1.8.d:
सदावगाह्य सलिले विशुद्धाः किं द्विजोत्तमाः
तस्मादाभ्यन्तरं शौचं सदा कार्यं विधानतः ॥
1.8.m: plunging constantly into water, become purified, O best of the twice-born? / Therefore, internal purity must always be performed according to rule.

1.8.s:
ātmajñānāmbhasi snātvā sakṛdālipya bhāvataḥ
suvairāgyamṛdā śuddhaḥ śaucamevaṃ prakīrtitam //
1.8.d:
आत्मज्ञानाम्भसि स्नात्वा सकृदालिप्य भावतः
सुवैराग्यमृदा शुद्धः शौचमेवं प्रकीर्तितम् ॥
1.8.m: Bathing in the water of knowledge of the Self, anointing oneself once through devotion / with the clay of true dispassion, one is pure; such is declared to be purity.

1.8.s:
śuddhasya siddhayo dṛṣṭā naivāśuddhasya siddhayaḥ
nyāyenāgatayā vṛttyā saṃtuṣṭo yastu suvrataḥ //
1.8.d:
शुद्धस्य सिद्धयो दृष्टा नैवाशुद्धस्य सिद्धयः
न्यायेनागतया वृत्त्या संतुष्टो यस्तु सुव्रतः ॥
1.8.m: Supernatural powers are seen in the pure, never are powers seen in the impure. / He who is of good vows, contented with a livelihood obtained righteously,

1.8.s:
saṃtoṣastasya satatam atītārthasya cāsmṛtiḥ
cāndrāyaṇādinipuṇas tapāṃsi suśubhāni ca //
1.8.d:
संतोषस्तस्य सततम् अतीतार्थस्य चास्मृतिः
चान्द्रायणादिनिपुणस् तपांसि सुशुभानि च ॥
1.8.m: has constant contentment, and non-remembrance of past things. / Skilled in [observances such as] the Cāndrāyaṇa fast, and most auspicious austerities,

1.8.s:
svādhyāyastu japaḥ proktaḥ praṇavasya tridhā smṛtaḥ
vācikaścādhamo mukhya upāṃśuścottamottamaḥ //
1.8.d:
स्वाध्यायस्तु जपः प्रोक्तः प्रणवस्य त्रिधा स्मृतः
वाचिकश्चाधमो मुख्य उपांशुश्चोत्तमोत्तमः ॥
1.8.m: self-study is declared as recitation; it is remembered as threefold for the Praṇava: / spoken aloud is the lowest, murmured is the principal, and mental is the highest of the high.

1.8.s:
mānaso vistareṇaiva kalpe pañcākṣare smṛtaḥ
tathā śivapraṇīdhānaṃ manovākkāyakarmaṇā //
1.8.d:
मानसो विस्तरेणैव कल्पे पञ्चाक्षरे स्मृतः
तथा शिवप्रणीधानं मनोवाक्कायकर्मणा ॥
1.8.m: In the ritual of the five-syllable [mantra] it is remembered in detail [as such]. / Likewise, devotion to Śiva through the action of mind, speech, and body,

1.8.s:
śivajñānaṃ gurorbhaktir acalā supratiṣṭhitā
nigraho hyapahṛtyāśu prasaktānīndriyāṇi ca //
1.8.d:
शिवज्ञानं गुरोर्भक्तिर् अचला सुप्रतिष्ठिता
निग्रहो ह्यपहृत्याशु प्रसक्तानीन्द्रियाणि च ॥
1.8.m: knowledge of Śiva, and unwavering, firmly established devotion to the guru. / For restraint is quickly pulling back the attached senses

1.8.s:
viṣayeṣu samāsena pratyāhāraḥ prakīrtitaḥ
cittasya dhāraṇā proktā sthānabandhaḥ samāsataḥ //
1.8.d:
विषयेषु समासेन प्रत्याहारः प्रकीर्तितः
चित्तस्य धारणा प्रोक्ता स्थानबन्धः समासतः ॥
1.8.m: from sense objects; in brief, it is proclaimed as withdrawal. / Concentration of the mind is declared in brief to be fixation on a spot.

1.8.s:
tasyāḥ svāsthyena dhyānaṃ ca samādhiś ca vicārataḥ
tatraikacittatā dhyānaṃ pratyayāntaravarjitam //
1.8.d:
तस्याः स्वास्थ्येन ध्यानं च समाधिश् च विचारतः
तत्रैकचित्तता ध्यानं प्रत्ययान्तरवर्जितम् ॥
1.8.m: Through its stability come meditation and absorption, upon examination. / There, meditation is one-pointedness of the mind, devoid of other mental notions.

1.8.s:
cidbhāsamarthamātrasya dehaśūnyamiva sthitam
samādhiḥ sarvahetuś ca prāṇāyāma iti smṛtaḥ //
1.8.d:
चिद्भासमर्थमात्रस्य देहशून्यमिव स्थितम्
समाधिः सर्वहेतुश् च प्राणायाम इति स्मृतः ॥
1.8.m: Absorption is the manifestation of consciousness as the object alone, standing as if empty of the body. / And breath-control is remembered as the cause of all [these].

1.8.s:
prāṇaḥ svadehajo vāyur yamastasya nirodhanam
tridhā dvijairyamaḥ prokto mando madhyottamas tathā //
1.8.d:
प्राणः स्वदेहजो वायुर् यमस्तस्य निरोधनम्
त्रिधा द्विजैर्यमः प्रोक्तो मन्दो मध्योत्तमस् तथा ॥
1.8.m: Prāṇa is the wind produced in one's body; restraint is its stoppage. / Restraint has been declared threefold by the twice-born: mild, middling, and superior.

1.8.s:
prāṇāpānanirodhastu prāṇāyāmaḥ prakīrtitaḥ
prāṇāyāmasya mānaṃ tu mātrādvādaśakaṃ smṛtam //
1.8.d:
प्राणापाननिरोधस्तु प्राणायामः प्रकीर्तितः
प्राणायामस्य मानं तु मात्राद्वादशकं स्मृतम् ॥
1.8.m: Breath-control is proclaimed to be the stoppage of prāṇa and apāna. / The measure of breath-control is remembered to be twelve mātrās.

1.8.s:
nīco dvādaśamātrastu uddhāto dvādaśaḥ smṛtaḥ
madhyamas tu dviruddhātaś caturviṃśatimātrakaḥ //
1.8.d:
नीचो द्वादशमात्रस्तु उद्धातो द्वादशः स्मृतः
मध्यमस् तु द्विरुद्धातश् चतुर्विंशतिमात्रकः ॥
1.8.m: The low is twelve mātrās, remembered as having twelve udghātas; / the middling has two udghātas, consisting of twenty-four mātrās;

1.8.s:
mukhyastu yastriruddhātaḥ ṣaṭtriṃśanmātra ucyate
prasvedakampanotthānajanakaśca yathākramam //
1.8.d:
मुख्यस्तु यस्त्रिरुद्धातः षट्त्रिंशन्मात्र उच्यते
प्रस्वेदकम्पनोत्थानजनकश्च यथाक्रमम् ॥
1.8.m: and the principal is said to have three udghātas, consisting of thirty-six mātrās, / producing perspiration, trembling, and rising up respectively.

1.8.s:
ānandodbhavayogārthaṃ nidrāghūrṇistathaiva ca
romāñcadhvanisaṃviddhasvāṅgamoṭanakampanam //
1.8.d:
आनन्दोद्भवयोगार्थं निद्राघूर्णिस्तथैव च
रोमाञ्चध्वनिसंविद्धस्वाङ्गमोटनकम्पनम् ॥
1.8.m: For the sake of yoga arising from bliss, there is sleepiness and reeling, / bristling of body hair, being penetrated by sound, stretching of one's limbs, trembling,

1.8.s:
bhramaṇaṃ svedajanyā sā saṃvinmūrchā bhavedyadā
tadottamottamaḥ proktaḥ prāṇāyāmaḥ suśobhanaḥ //
1.8.d:
भ्रमणं स्वेदजन्या सा संविन्मूर्छा भवेद्यदा
तदोत्तमोत्तमः प्रोक्तः प्राणायामः सुशोभनः ॥
1.8.m: spinning, and when that swooning of consciousness born of sweating occurs, / then that breath-control is declared most excellent and very auspicious.

1.8.s:
sagarbho 'garbha ityuktaḥ sajapo vijapaḥ kramāt
ibho vā śarabho vāpi durādharṣo 'tha kesarī //
1.8.d:
सगर्भो ऽगर्भ इत्युक्तः सजपो विजपः क्रमात्
इभो वा शरभो वापि दुराधर्षो ऽथ केसरी ॥
1.8.m: It is spoken of as with-seed and seedless, respectively with mantra-recitation and without mantra-recitation. / Just as an elephant, a śarabha, or an unconquerable lion,

1.8.s:
gṛhīto damyamānastu yathāsvasthastu jāyate
tathā samīraṇo 'svastho durādharṣaś ca yoginām //
1.8.d:
गृहीतो दम्यमानस्तु यथास्वस्थस्तु जायते
तथा समीरणो ऽस्वस्थो दुराधर्षश् च योगिनाम् ॥
1.8.m: when captured and being tamed, becomes quieted, / so the unruly and unconquerable wind of yogins,

1.8.s:
nyāyataḥ sevyamānastu sa evaṃ svasthatāṃ vrajet
yathaiva mṛgarāṅnāgaḥ śarabho vāpi durmadaḥ //
1.8.d:
न्यायतः सेव्यमानस्तु स एवं स्वस्थतां व्रजेत्
यथैव मृगराङ्नागः शरभो वापि दुर्मदः ॥
1.8.m: when cultivated properly, attains calmness in this way. / Just as the king of beasts, an elephant, or even a furious śarabha,

1.8.s:
kālāntaravaśādyogād damyate paramādarāt
tathā paricayātsvāsthyaṃ samatvaṃ cādhigacchati //
1.8.d:
कालान्तरवशाद्योगाद् दम्यते परमादरात्
तथा परिचयात्स्वास्थ्यं समत्वं चाधिगच्छति ॥
1.8.m: over the course of time through practice is tamed with utmost care, / so through familiarity does it attain calmness and equanimity.

1.8.s:
yogādabhyasate yastu vyasanaṃ naiva jāyate
evamabhyasyamānastu muneḥ prāṇo vinirdahet //
1.8.d:
योगादभ्यसते यस्तु व्यसनं नैव जायते
एवमभ्यस्यमानस्तु मुनेः प्राणो विनिर्दहेत् ॥
1.8.m: For one who practices through yoga, no misfortune arises. / When practiced in this manner, the sage's breath burns away

1.8.s:
manovākkāyajān doṣān karturdehaṃ ca rakṣati
saṃyuktasya tathā samyak prāṇāyāmena dhīmataḥ //
1.8.d:
मनोवाक्कायजान् दोषान् कर्तुर्देहं च रक्षति
संयुक्तस्य तथा सम्यक् प्राणायामेन धीमतः ॥
1.8.m: defects born of mind, speech, and body, and protects the body of the practitioner. / Thus, for the wise one properly endowed with breath-control,

1.8.s:
doṣāttasmācca naśyanti niśvāsastena jīryate
prāṇāyāmena sidhyanti divyāḥ śāntyādayaḥ kramāt //
1.8.d:
दोषात्तस्माच्च नश्यन्ति निश्वासस्तेन जीर्यते
प्राणायामेन सिध्यन्ति दिव्याः शान्त्यादयः क्रमात् ॥
1.8.m: defects are destroyed on account of it, and by it breathing is digested. / Through breath-control, the divine [qualities] such as peace are accomplished in turn:

1.8.s:
śāntiḥ praśāntirdīptiś ca prasādaś ca tathā kramāt
ādau catuṣṭayasyeha proktā śāntiriha dvijāḥ //
1.8.d:
शान्तिः प्रशान्तिर्दीप्तिश् च प्रसादश् च तथा क्रमात्
आदौ चतुष्टयस्येह प्रोक्ता शान्तिरिह द्विजाः ॥
1.8.m: peace, profound calm, illumination, and serenity, in that order. / Here, among the four, peace is declared first, O twice-born;

1.8.s:
sahajāgantukānāṃ ca pāpānāṃ śāntir ucyate
praśāntiḥ saṃyamaḥ samyag vacasāmiti saṃsmṛtā //
1.8.d:
सहजागन्तुकानां च पापानां शान्तिर् उच्यते
प्रशान्तिः संयमः सम्यग् वचसामिति संस्मृता ॥
1.8.m: it is said to be the appeasement of innate and adventitious sins. / Profound calm is well remembered to be the complete restraint of speech.

1.8.s:
prakāśo dīptirityuktaḥ sarvataḥ sarvadā dvijāḥ
sarvendriyaprasādastu buddhervai marutāmapi //
1.8.d:
प्रकाशो दीप्तिरित्युक्तः सर्वतः सर्वदा द्विजाः
सर्वेन्द्रियप्रसादस्तु बुद्धेर्वै मरुतामपि ॥
1.8.m: Illumination is declared to be light on all sides and at all times, O twice-born. / The serenity of all senses, of the intellect, and also of the winds,

1.8.s:
prasāda iti samproktaḥ svānte tviha catuṣṭaye
prāṇo 'pānaḥ samānaś ca udāno vyāna eva ca //
1.8.d:
प्रसाद इति सम्प्रोक्तः स्वान्ते त्विह चतुष्टये
प्राणो ऽपानः समानश् च उदानो व्यान एव च ॥
1.8.m: is proclaimed as serenity here at the end of the four. / Prāṇa, apāna, samāna, udāna, and vyāna,

1.8.s:
nāgaḥ kūrmastu kṛkalo devadatto dhanaṃjayaḥ
eteṣāṃ yaḥ prasādastu marutāmiti saṃsmṛtaḥ //
1.8.d:
नागः कूर्मस्तु कृकलो देवदत्तो धनंजयः
एतेषां यः प्रसादस्तु मरुतामिति संस्मृतः ॥
1.8.m: nāga, kūrma, kṛkala, devadatta, and dhanaṃjaya— / the serenity of these winds is what is remembered.

1.8.s:
prayāṇaṃ kurute tasmād vāyuḥ prāṇa iti smṛtaḥ
apānayatyapānastu āhārādīn krameṇa ca //
1.8.d:
प्रयाणं कुरुते तस्माद् वायुः प्राण इति स्मृतः
अपानयत्यपानस्तु आहारादीन् क्रमेण च ॥
1.8.m: Because it makes departures, the wind is remembered as prāṇa; / apāna carries downward food and other things in sequence;

1.8.s:
vyāno vyānāmayatyaṅgaṃ vyādhyādīnāṃ prakopakaḥ
udvejayati marmāṇi udāno 'yaṃ prakīrtitaḥ //
1.8.d:
व्यानो व्यानामयत्यङ्गं व्याध्यादीनां प्रकोपकः
उद्वेजयति मर्माणि उदानो ऽयं प्रकीर्तितः ॥
1.8.m: vyāna pervades the body, provoking diseases and the like; / udāna is proclaimed as that which agitates the vital points.

1.8.s:
samaṃ nayati gātrāṇi samānaḥ pañca vāyavaḥ
udgāre nāga ākhyātaḥ kūrma unmīlane tu saḥ //
1.8.d:
समं नयति गात्राणि समानः पञ्च वायवः
उद्गारे नाग आख्यातः कूर्म उन्मीलने तु सः ॥
1.8.m: Samāna brings the limbs into equilibrium; these are the five vital airs. / Nāga is declared to cause belching, and Kūrma causes the opening of the eyes;

1.8.s:
kṛkalaḥ kṣutakāyaiva devadatto vijṛmbhaṇe
dhanaṃjayo mahāghoṣaḥ sarvagaḥ sa mṛte 'pi hi //
1.8.d:
कृकलः क्षुतकायैव देवदत्तो विजृम्भणे
धनंजयो महाघोषः सर्वगः स मृते ऽपि हि ॥
1.8.m: Kṛkala is for sneezing, Devadatta for yawning, / and Dhanañjaya of great sound is omnipresent; indeed, he remains even when one is dead.

1.8.s:
iti yo daśavāyūnāṃ prāṇāyāmena sidhyati
prasādo 'sya turīyā tu saṃjñā viprāścatuṣṭaye //
1.8.d:
इति यो दशवायूनां प्राणायामेन सिध्यति
प्रसादो ऽस्य तुरीया तु संज्ञा विप्राश्चतुष्टये ॥
1.8.m: Thus, what is mastered by means of prāṇāyāma over the ten vital airs / is its serenity; and its fourth designation, O brāhmaṇas, in the tetrad [is prasāda].

1.8.s:
visvarastu mahān prajño mano brahmā citiḥ smṛtiḥ
khyātiḥ saṃvittataḥ paścād īśvaro matireva ca //
1.8.d:
विस्वरस्तु महान् प्रज्ञो मनो ब्रह्मा चितिः स्मृतिः
ख्यातिः संवित्ततः पश्चाद् ईश्वरो मतिरेव च ॥
1.8.m: Visvara, Mahat, Prajñā, Manas, Brahmā, Citi, Smṛti, / Khyāti, Saṃvid, and thereafter Īśvara and Mati:

1.8.s:
buddheretāḥ dvijāḥ saṃjñā mahataḥ parikīrtitāḥ
asyā buddheḥ prasādastu prāṇāyāmena sidhyati //
1.8.d:
बुद्धेरेताः द्विजाः संज्ञा महतः परिकीर्तिताः
अस्या बुद्धेः प्रसादस्तु प्राणायामेन सिध्यति ॥
1.8.m: these, O twice-born, are proclaimed as names of Buddhi, the Mahat. / And serenity of this Buddhi is achieved through prāṇāyāma.

1.8.s:
visvaro visvarībhāvo dvaṃdvānāṃ munisattamāḥ
agrajaḥ sarvatattvānāṃ mahānyaḥ parimāṇataḥ //
1.8.d:
विस्वरो विस्वरीभावो द्वंद्वानां मुनिसत्तमाः
अग्रजः सर्वतत्त्वानां महान्यः परिमाणतः ॥
1.8.m: Visvara means the dissolution of the pairs of opposites, O best of sages; / Mahat is the first-born of all principles, great in measure;

1.8.s:
yatpramāṇaguhā prajñā manastu manute yataḥ
bṛhattvād bṛṃhaṇatvācca brahmā brahmavidāṃvarāḥ //
1.8.d:
यत्प्रमाणगुहा प्रज्ञा मनस्तु मनुते यतः
बृहत्त्वाद् बृंहणत्वाच्च ब्रह्मा ब्रह्मविदांवराः ॥
1.8.m: Prajñā is so called because it is the cavern of valid knowledge; Manas because it conceptualises; / Brahmā because of greatness and expansion, O best of knowers of Brahman;

1.8.s:
sarvakarmāṇi bhogārthaṃ yaccinoti citiḥ smṛtā
smarate yatsmṛtiḥ sarvaṃ saṃvidvai vindate yataḥ //
1.8.d:
सर्वकर्माणि भोगार्थं यच्चिनोति चितिः स्मृता
स्मरते यत्स्मृतिः सर्वं संविद्वै विन्दते यतः ॥
1.8.m: it is remembered as Citi because it gathers all deeds for enjoyment; / it is Smṛti because it remembers everything; it is Saṃvid because it finds;

1.8.s:
khyāyate yattviti khyātir jñānādibhir anekaśaḥ
sarvatattvādhipaḥ sarvaṃ vijānāti yadīśvaraḥ //
1.8.d:
ख्यायते यत्त्विति ख्यातिर् ज्ञानादिभिर् अनेकशः
सर्वतत्त्वाधिपः सर्वं विजानाति यदीश्वरः ॥
1.8.m: it is Khyāti because it is revealed in many ways through knowledge and the like; / it is Īśvara because it is the lord of all principles and knows everything;

1.8.s:
manute manyate yasmān matirmatimatāṃvarāḥ
arthaṃ bodhayate yacca budhyate buddhirucyate //
1.8.d:
मनुते मन्यते यस्मान् मतिर्मतिमतांवराः
अर्थं बोधयते यच्च बुध्यते बुद्धिरुच्यते ॥
1.8.m: it is Mati because it thinks and understands, O best of the wise; / and it is called Buddhi because it awakens to and understands the object.

1.8.s:
asyā buddheḥ prasādastu prāṇāyāmena sidhyati
doṣānvinirdahetsarvān prāṇāyāmādasau yamī //
1.8.d:
अस्या बुद्धेः प्रसादस्तु प्राणायामेन सिध्यति
दोषान्विनिर्दहेत्सर्वान् प्राणायामादसौ यमी ॥
1.8.m: Serenity of this intellect is achieved through prāṇāyāma. / Through prāṇāyāma the self-controlled yogin burns away all defects;

1.8.s:
pātakaṃ dhāraṇābhistu pratyāhāreṇa nirdahet
viṣayānviṣavaddhyātvā dhyānenānīśvarān guṇān //
1.8.d:
पातकं धारणाभिस्तु प्रत्याहारेण निर्दहेत्
विषयान्विषवद्ध्यात्वा ध्यानेनानीश्वरान् गुणान् ॥
1.8.m: through dhāraṇās he burns away sin; through pratyāhāra / he burns away sensory objects, contemplating them like poison; through dhyāna [he burns away] the non-sovereign guṇas;

1.8.s:
samādhinā yatiśreṣṭhāḥ prajñāvṛddhiṃ vivardhayet
sthānaṃ labdhvaiva kurvīta yogāṣṭāṅgāni vai kramāt //
1.8.d:
समाधिना यतिश्रेष्ठाः प्रज्ञावृद्धिं विवर्धयेत्
स्थानं लब्ध्वैव कुर्वीत योगाष्टाङ्गानि वै क्रमात् ॥
1.8.m: through samādhi, O best of ascetics, he increases the growth of wisdom. / Only after securing a suitable place should he practise the eight limbs of yoga in succession.

1.8.s:
labdhvāsanāni vidhivad yogasiddhyartham ātmavit
ādeśakāle yogasya darśanaṃ hi na vidyate //
1.8.d:
लब्ध्वासनानि विधिवद् योगसिद्ध्यर्थम् आत्मवित्
आदेशकाले योगस्य दर्शनं हि न विद्यते ॥
1.8.m: Having obtained a posture according to rule, for the attainment of yoga, the knower of the Self [should practise]; / for yoga cannot be perceived in an unfit place or time:

1.8.s:
agnyabhyāse jale vāpi śuṣkaparṇacaye tathā
jantuvyāpte śmaśāne ca jīrṇagoṣṭhe catuṣpathe //
1.8.d:
अग्न्यभ्यासे जले वापि शुष्कपर्णचये तथा
जन्तुव्याप्ते श्मशाने च जीर्णगोष्ठे चतुष्पथे ॥
1.8.m: near a fire, in water, on a heap of dry leaves, / in a place infested with vermin, in a cremation ground, in a ruined cow-pen, at a crossroads,

1.8.s:
saśabde sabhaye vāpi caityavalmīkasaṃcaye
aśubhe durjanākrānte maśakādisamanvite //
1.8.d:
सशब्दे सभये वापि चैत्यवल्मीकसंचये
अशुभे दुर्जनाक्रान्ते मशकादिसमन्विते ॥
1.8.m: in a noisy or frightening place, near a caitya or a collection of anthills, / in an inauspicious place, in a place overrun by wicked men, or one full of mosquitoes and the like;

1.8.s:
nācareddehabādhāyāṃ daurmanasyādisambhave
sugupte tu śubhe ramye guhāyāṃ parvatasya tu //
1.8.d:
नाचरेद्देहबाधायां दौर्मनस्यादिसम्भवे
सुगुप्ते तु शुभे रम्ये गुहायां पर्वतस्य तु ॥
1.8.m: he should not practise when afflicted in body, or when depression and the like arise; / but in a well-concealed, auspicious, delightful mountain cave,

1.8.s:
bhavakṣetre sugupte vā bhavārāme vane 'pi vā
gṛhe tu suśubhe deśe vijane jantuvarjite //
1.8.d:
भवक्षेत्रे सुगुप्ते वा भवारामे वने ऽपि वा
गृहे तु सुशुभे देशे विजने जन्तुवर्जिते ॥
1.8.m: or in a well-concealed sacred precinct of Bhava, in a park of Bhava, or in a forest, / or in a house in a very auspicious locality, secluded and free from creatures,

1.8.s:
atyantanirmale samyak supralipte vicitrite
darpaṇodarasaṃkāśe kṛṣṇāgarusudhūpite //
1.8.d:
अत्यन्तनिर्मले सम्यक् सुप्रलिप्ते विचित्रिते
दर्पणोदरसंकाशे कृष्णागरुसुधूपिते ॥
1.8.m: exceedingly clean, well-smeared, beautifully decorated, / smooth like the surface of a mirror, perfumed with black agarwood incense,

1.8.s:
nānāpuṣpasamākīrṇe vitānopari śobhite
phalapallavamūlāḍhye kuśapuṣpasamanvite //
1.8.d:
नानापुष्पसमाकीर्णे वितानोपरि शोभिते
फलपल्लवमूलाढ्ये कुशपुष्पसमन्विते ॥
1.8.m: strewn with various flowers, adorned with a canopy above, / abundant in fruits, sprouts, and roots, provided with kuśa grass and flowers.

1.8.s:
samāsanastho yogāṅgāny abhyaseddhṛṣitaḥ svayam
praṇipatya guruṃ paścād bhavaṃ devīṃ vināyakam //
1.8.d:
समासनस्थो योगाङ्गान्य् अभ्यसेद्धृषितः स्वयम्
प्रणिपत्य गुरुं पश्चाद् भवं देवीं विनायकम् ॥
1.8.m: Seated on a level seat, joyful, he should himself practise the limbs of yoga. / Having first bowed down to the guru, and then to Bhava, the Goddess, and Vināyaka,

1.8.s:
yogīśvarān saśiṣyāṃś ca yogaṃ yuñjīta yogavit
āsanaṃ svastikaṃ baddhvā padmamardhāsanaṃ tu vā //
1.8.d:
योगीश्वरान् सशिष्यांश् च योगं युञ्जीत योगवित्
आसनं स्वस्तिकं बद्ध्वा पद्ममर्धासनं तु वा ॥
1.8.m: and to the lords of yoga along with their disciples, the knower of yoga should unite in yoga. / Having assumed the svastika posture, or the lotus posture, or the half-posture,

1.8.s:
samajānus tathā dhīmān ekajānurathāpivā
samaṃ dṛḍhāsano bhūtvā saṃhṛtya caraṇāvubhau //
1.8.d:
समजानुस् तथा धीमान् एकजानुरथापिवा
समं दृढासनो भूत्वा संहृत्य चरणावुभौ ॥
1.8.m: the wise practitioner, with knees level or with one knee [raised], / having become firm in his seat and level, drawing in both feet,

1.8.s:
saṃvṛtāsyopabaddhākṣa uro viṣṭabhya cāgrataḥ
pārṣṇibhyāṃ vṛṣaṇau rakṣaṃs tathā prajananaṃ punaḥ //
1.8.d:
संवृतास्योपबद्धाक्ष उरो विष्टभ्य चाग्रतः
पार्ष्णिभ्यां वृषणौ रक्षंस् तथा प्रजननं पुनः ॥
1.8.m: with mouth closed, eyes steady, chest held erect in front, / protecting both testicles and the organ of generation with his heels,

1.8.s:
kiṃcidunnāmitaśira dantairdantānna saṃspṛśet
samprekṣya nāsikāgraṃ svaṃ diśaścānavalokayan //
1.8.d:
किंचिदुन्नामितशिर दन्तैर्दन्तान्न संस्पृशेत्
सम्प्रेक्ष्य नासिकाग्रं स्वं दिशश्चानवलोकयन् ॥
1.8.m: with head slightly raised, not letting teeth touch teeth, / gazing at the tip of his own nose and not looking at the directions,

1.8.s:
tamaḥ pracchādya rajasā rajaḥ sattvena chādayet
tataḥ sattvasthito bhūtvā śivadhyānaṃ samabhyaset //
1.8.d:
तमः प्रच्छाद्य रजसा रजः सत्त्वेन छादयेत्
ततः सत्त्वस्थितो भूत्वा शिवध्यानं समभ्यसेत् ॥
1.8.m: having covered tamas with rajas, he should cover rajas with sattva; / then, established in sattva, he should practise meditation on Śiva.

1.8.s:
oṃkāravācyaṃ paramaṃ śuddhaṃ dīpaśikhākṛtim
dhyāyedvai puṇḍarīkasya karṇikāyāṃ samāhitaḥ //
1.8.d:
ओंकारवाच्यं परमं शुद्धं दीपशिखाकृतिम्
ध्यायेद्वै पुण्डरीकस्य कर्णिकायां समाहितः ॥
1.8.m: He should meditate with concentrated mind upon the supreme, pure [reality] signified by the syllable Oṃ, / having the form of a lamp's flame, in the pericarp of the lotus.

1.8.s:
nābheradhastādvā vidvān dhyātvā kamalamuttamam
tryaṅgule cāṣṭakoṇaṃ vā pañcakoṇamathāpi vā //
1.8.d:
नाभेरधस्ताद्वा विद्वान् ध्यात्वा कमलमुत्तमम्
त्र्यङ्गुले चाष्टकोणं वा पञ्चकोणमथापि वा ॥
1.8.m: Or, beneath the navel, the wise man, having meditated on the supreme lotus / at a distance of three aṅgulas, eight-cornered, or five-cornered,

1.8.s:
trikoṇaṃ ca tathāgneyaṃ saumyaṃ sauraṃ svaśaktibhiḥ
sauraṃ saumya tathāgneyam atha vānukrameṇa tu //
1.8.d:
त्रिकोणं च तथाग्नेयं सौम्यं सौरं स्वशक्तिभिः
सौरं सौम्य तथाग्नेयम् अथ वानुक्रमेण तु ॥
1.8.m: and triangular—related to fire, the moon, and the sun along with their respective powers; / or in the sequence of solar, lunar, and fiery;

1.8.s:
āgneyaṃ ca tataḥ sauraṃ saumyamevaṃ vidhānataḥ
agneradhaḥ prakalpyaivaṃ dharmādīnāṃ catuṣṭayam //
1.8.d:
आग्नेयं च ततः सौरं सौम्यमेवं विधानतः
अग्नेरधः प्रकल्प्यैवं धर्मादीनां चतुष्टयम् ॥
1.8.m: or fiery, then solar, and lunar, according to rule; / having thus projected beneath the fire the tetrad of dharma and the rest,

1.8.s:
guṇatrayaṃ krameṇaiva maṇḍalopari bhāvayet
sattvasthaṃ cintayedrudraṃ svaśaktyā parimaṇḍitam //
1.8.d:
गुणत्रयं क्रमेणैव मण्डलोपरि भावयेत्
सत्त्वस्थं चिन्तयेद्रुद्रं स्वशक्त्या परिमण्डितम् ॥
1.8.m: he should contemplate the triad of guṇas in order above the maṇḍala. / He should meditate on Rudra seated in sattva, surrounded by His own power.

1.8.s:
nābhau vātha gale vāpi bhrūmadhye vā yathāvidhi
lalāṭaphalikāyāṃ vā mūrdhni dhyānaṃ samācaret //
1.8.d:
नाभौ वाथ गले वापि भ्रूमध्ये वा यथाविधि
ललाटफलिकायां वा मूर्ध्नि ध्यानं समाचरेत् ॥
1.8.m: Either at the navel, or in the throat, or between the eyebrows according to rule, / or on the forehead plate, or at the crown of the head, he should perform meditation:

1.8.s:
dvidale ṣoḍaśāre vā dvādaśāre krameṇa tu
daśāre vā ṣaḍasre vā caturasre smarecchivam //
1.8.d:
द्विदले षोडशारे वा द्वादशारे क्रमेण तु
दशारे वा षडस्रे वा चतुरस्रे स्मरेच्छिवम् ॥
1.8.m: in the two-petalled, or sixteen-spoked, or twelve-spoked [lotus] in order, / or ten-spoked, or hexagonal, or four-cornered, he should remember Śiva,

1.8.s:
kanakābhe tathāgārasaṃnibhe susite 'pi vā
dvādaśādityasaṃkāśe candrabimbasame 'pi vā //
1.8.d:
कनकाभे तथागारसंनिभे सुसिते ऽपि वा
द्वादशादित्यसंकाशे चन्द्रबिम्बसमे ऽपि वा ॥
1.8.m: radiant like gold, or resembling an ember, or exceedingly white, / resembling twelve suns, or equal to the disc of the moon,

1.8.s:
vidyutkoṭinibhe sthāne cintayetparameśvaram
agnivarṇe 'thavā vidyud valayābhe samāhitaḥ //
1.8.d:
विद्युत्कोटिनिभे स्थाने चिन्तयेत्परमेश्वरम्
अग्निवर्णे ऽथवा विद्युद् वलयाभे समाहितः ॥
1.8.m: in a place resembling ten million lightnings, he should contemplate the Supreme Lord; / or concentrated [on Him] fire-coloured, or resembling a circle of lightning,

1.8.s:
vajrakoṭiprabhe sthāne padmarāganibhe 'pi vā
nīlalohitabimbe vā yogī dhyānaṃ samabhyaset //
1.8.d:
वज्रकोटिप्रभे स्थाने पद्मरागनिभे ऽपि वा
नीललोहितबिम्बे वा योगी ध्यानं समभ्यसेत् ॥
1.8.m: in a place shining like ten million thunderbolts, or resembling a ruby, / or in the disc of Nīlalohita, the yogin should practise meditation.

1.8.s:
maheśvaraṃ hṛdi dhyāyen nābhipadme sadāśivam
candracūḍaṃ lalāṭe tu bhrūmadhye śaṃkaraṃ svayam //
1.8.d:
महेश्वरं हृदि ध्यायेन् नाभिपद्मे सदाशिवम्
चन्द्रचूडं ललाटे तु भ्रूमध्ये शंकरं स्वयम् ॥
1.8.m: He should meditate on Maheśvara in the heart, on Sadāśiva in the navel lotus, / on the Moon-crested Lord in the forehead, and on Śaṅkara Himself between the eyebrows;

1.8.s:
divye ca śāśvatasthāne śivadhyānaṃ samabhyaset
nirmalaṃ niṣkalaṃ brahma suśāntaṃ jñānarūpiṇam //
1.8.d:
दिव्ये च शाश्वतस्थाने शिवध्यानं समभ्यसेत्
निर्मलं निष्कलं ब्रह्म सुशान्तं ज्ञानरूपिणम् ॥
1.8.m: and in the divine and eternal place he should practise meditation on Śiva: / spotless, partless Brahman, tranquil, of the nature of knowledge,

1.8.s:
alakṣaṇamanirdeśyam aṇoralpataraṃ śubham
nirālambam atarkyaṃ ca vināśotpattivarjitam //
1.8.d:
अलक्षणमनिर्देश्यम् अणोरल्पतरं शुभम्
निरालम्बम् अतर्क्यं च विनाशोत्पत्तिवर्जितम् ॥
1.8.m: without distinguishing marks, undefinable, smaller than the atom, auspicious, / without support, incomprehensible, devoid of destruction and origination,

1.8.s:
kaivalyaṃ caiva nirvāṇaṃ niḥśreyasam anuttamam
amṛtaṃ cākṣaraṃ brahma hy apunarbhavam adbhutam //
1.8.d:
कैवल्यं चैव निर्वाणं निःश्रेयसम् अनुत्तमम्
अमृतं चाक्षरं ब्रह्म ह्य् अपुनर्भवम् अद्भुतम् ॥
1.8.m: absolute liberation, nirvāṇa, the unsurpassed supreme good, / the immortal and imperishable Brahman, wondrous, free from rebirth,

1.8.s:
mahānandaṃ parānandaṃ yogānandamanāmayam
heyopādeyarahitaṃ sūkṣmātsūkṣmataraṃ śivam //
1.8.d:
महानन्दं परानन्दं योगानन्दमनामयम्
हेयोपादेयरहितं सूक्ष्मात्सूक्ष्मतरं शिवम् ॥
1.8.m: great bliss, supreme bliss, the healthy bliss of yoga, / free from things to be abandoned or accepted, subtler than the subtlest, Śiva,

1.8.s:
svayaṃvedyamavedyaṃ tac chivaṃ jñānamayaṃ param
atīndriyam anābhāsaṃ paraṃ tattvaṃ parātparam //
1.8.d:
स्वयंवेद्यमवेद्यं तच् छिवं ज्ञानमयं परम्
अतीन्द्रियम् अनाभासं परं तत्त्वं परात्परम् ॥
1.8.m: known by Himself, unknowable [by others], that Śiva consisting of knowledge, supreme, / beyond the senses, devoid of appearance, the supreme reality, higher than the highest,

1.8.s:
sarvopādhivinirmuktaṃ dhyānagamyaṃ vicārataḥ
advayaṃ tamasaścaiva parastātsaṃsthitaṃ param //
1.8.d:
सर्वोपाधिविनिर्मुक्तं ध्यानगम्यं विचारतः
अद्वयं तमसश्चैव परस्तात्संस्थितं परम् ॥
1.8.m: completely free from all limiting conditions, accessible through meditation and reflection, / non-dual, established beyond darkness, supreme.

1.8.s:
manasyevaṃ mahādevaṃ hṛtpadme vāpi cintayet
nābhau sadāśivaṃ cāpi sarvadevātmakaṃ vibhum //
1.8.d:
मनस्येवं महादेवं हृत्पद्मे वापि चिन्तयेत्
नाभौ सदाशिवं चापि सर्वदेवात्मकं विभुम् ॥
1.8.m: Thus he should contemplate Mahādeva in the mind, or in the lotus of the heart; / and in the navel [he should contemplate] Sadāśiva, the all-pervading soul of all gods;

1.8.s:
dehamadhye śivaṃ devaṃ śuddhajñānamayaṃ vibhum
kanyasenaiva mārgeṇa codghātenāpi śaṃkaram //
1.8.d:
देहमध्ये शिवं देवं शुद्धज्ञानमयं विभुम्
कन्यसेनैव मार्गेण चोद्घातेनापि शंकरम् ॥
1.8.m: in the middle of the body [he should contemplate] Lord Śiva, the all-pervading one consisting of pure knowledge. / Through the lowest path, and with expulsion, [he should meditate on] Śaṅkara;

1.8.s:
kramaśaḥ kanyasenaiva madhyamenāpi suvrataḥ
uttamenāpi vai vidvān kumbhakena samabhyaset //
1.8.d:
क्रमशः कन्यसेनैव मध्यमेनापि सुव्रतः
उत्तमेनापि वै विद्वान् कुम्भकेन समभ्यसेत् ॥
1.8.m: gradually, through the lowest, then the intermediate, O you of good vows, / and through the highest [breath-retention], the wise man should practise with kumbhaka.

1.8.s:
dvātriṃśad recayeddhīmān hṛdi nābhau samāhitaḥ
recakaṃ pūrakaṃ tyaktvā kumbhakaṃ ca dvijottamāḥ //
1.8.d:
द्वात्रिंशद् रेचयेद्धीमान् हृदि नाभौ समाहितः
रेचकं पूरकं त्यक्त्वा कुम्भकं च द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
1.8.m: Concentrated in the heart and the navel, the wise man should exhale thirty-two [measures]. / Having abandoned recaka, pūraka, and kumbhaka, O best of the twice-born,

1.8.s:
sākṣātsamarasenaiva dehamadhye smarecchivam
ekībhāvaṃ sametyaivaṃ tatra yadrasasambhavam //
1.8.d:
साक्षात्समरसेनैव देहमध्ये स्मरेच्छिवम्
एकीभावं समेत्यैवं तत्र यद्रससम्भवम् ॥
1.8.m: he should remember Śiva in the middle of the body directly through homogeneous essence, / thus having attained oneness through the essence that is produced there.

1.8.s:
ānandaṃ brahmaṇo vidvān sākṣātsamarase sthitaḥ
dhāraṇā dvādaśāyāmā dhyānaṃ dvādaśa dhāraṇam //
1.8.d:
आनन्दं ब्रह्मणो विद्वान् साक्षात्समरसे स्थितः
धारणा द्वादशायामा ध्यानं द्वादश धारणम् ॥
1.8.m: The wise man who stands directly in the uniform essence knows the bliss of Brahman. / Dhāraṇā lasts twelve breath-controls; dhyāna is twelve dhāraṇās.

1.8.s:
dhyānaṃ dvādaśakaṃ yāvat samādhir abhidhīyate
athavā jñānināṃ viprāḥ samparkādeva jāyate //
1.8.d:
ध्यानं द्वादशकं यावत् समाधिर् अभिधीयते
अथवा ज्ञानिनां विप्राः सम्पर्कादेव जायते ॥
1.8.m: A measure of twelve dhyānas is called samādhi. / Or, O brahmins, it arises for the wise simply through contact [with the Self],

1.8.s:
prayatnādvā tayostulyaṃ cirādvā hyacirāddvijāḥ
yogāntarāyās tasyātha jāyante yuñjataḥ punaḥ //
1.8.d:
प्रयत्नाद्वा तयोस्तुल्यं चिराद्वा ह्यचिराद्द्विजाः
योगान्तरायास् तस्याथ जायन्ते युञ्जतः पुनः ॥
1.8.m: or through effort equal to both, after a long time or quickly, O twice-born. / Then, obstacles to yoga arise again for him as he applies himself;

1.8.s: naśyanty abhyāsatas te 'pi praṇidhānena vai guroḥ //
1.8.d: नश्यन्त्य् अभ्यासतस् ते ऽपि प्रणिधानेन वै गुरोः ॥
1.8.m: yet they perish through practice and through devotion to the Guru.

1.9.s:
sūta uvāca
ālasyaṃ prathamaṃ paścād vyādhipīḍā prajāyate
pramādaḥ saṃśayasthāne cittasyehānavasthitiḥ //
1.9.d:
सूत उवाच
आलस्यं प्रथमं पश्चाद् व्याधिपीडा प्रजायते
प्रमादः संशयस्थाने चित्तस्येहानवस्थितिः ॥
1.9.m: Sūta said: / First is sloth; thereafter affliction by disease arises; / carelessness; doubt regarding the foundation; unsteadiness of the mind here;

1.9.s:
aśraddhādarśanaṃ bhrāntir duḥkhaṃ ca trividhaṃ tataḥ
daurmanasyamayogyeṣu viṣayeṣu ca yogyatā //
1.9.d:
अश्रद्धादर्शनं भ्रान्तिर् दुःखं च त्रिविधं ततः
दौर्मनस्यमयोग्येषु विषयेषु च योग्यता ॥
1.9.m: lack of faith; erroneous vision; and then threefold suffering; / depression; and inclination toward unsuitable objects—

1.9.s:
daśadhābhiprajāyante muneryogāntarāyakāḥ
ālasyaṃ cāpravṛttiś ca gurutvātkāyacittayoḥ //
1.9.d:
दशधाभिप्रजायन्ते मुनेर्योगान्तरायकाः
आलस्यं चाप्रवृत्तिश् च गुरुत्वात्कायचित्तयोः ॥
1.9.m: in ten ways do obstacles to yoga arise for the sage. / Sloth is lack of engagement due to heaviness of the body and mind.

1.9.s:
vyādhayo dhātuvaiṣamyāt karmajā doṣajās tathā
pramādastu samādhestu sādhanānām abhāvanam //
1.9.d:
व्याधयो धातुवैषम्यात् कर्मजा दोषजास् तथा
प्रमादस्तु समाधेस्तु साधनानाम् अभावनम् ॥
1.9.m: Diseases arise from imbalance of the humours, from past actions, or from the bodily faults. / Carelessness is the non-cultivation of the means to samādhi.

1.9.s:
idaṃ vetyubhayaspṛktaṃ vijñānaṃ sthānasaṃśayaḥ
anavasthitacittatvam apratiṣṭhā hi yoginaḥ //
1.9.d:
इदं वेत्युभयस्पृक्तं विज्ञानं स्थानसंशयः
अनवस्थितचित्तत्वम् अप्रतिष्ठा हि योगिनः ॥
1.9.m: Knowledge touching both alternatives—'Is it this or that?'—is doubt regarding the foundation. / Unsteadiness of the mind is indeed the yogin's lack of firm resting-place,

1.9.s:
labdhāyāmapi bhūmau ca cittasya bhavabandhanāt
aśraddhābhāvarahitā vṛttirvai sādhaneṣu ca //
1.9.d:
लब्धायामपि भूमौ च चित्तस्य भवबन्धनात्
अश्रद्धाभावरहिता वृत्तिर्वै साधनेषु च ॥
1.9.m: even when the plane has been attained, due to the mind's bond to worldly existence. / Lack of faith is a disposition devoid of trust toward the means,

1.9.s:
sādhye cittasya hi gurau jñānācāraśivādiṣu
viparyayajñānamiti bhrāntidarśanam ucyate //
1.9.d:
साध्ये चित्तस्य हि गुरौ ज्ञानाचारशिवादिषु
विपर्ययज्ञानमिति भ्रान्तिदर्शनम् उच्यते ॥
1.9.m: toward the goal, the mind, the Guru, wisdom, right conduct, Śiva, and the like. / Perverted knowledge is called erroneous vision.

1.9.s:
anātmanyātmavijñānam ajñānāttasya saṃnidhau
duḥkhamādhyātmikaṃ proktaṃ tathā caivādhibhautikam //
1.9.d:
अनात्मन्यात्मविज्ञानम् अज्ञानात्तस्य संनिधौ
दुःखमाध्यात्मिकं प्रोक्तं तथा चैवाधिभौतिकम् ॥
1.9.m: It is the cognition of the Self in the non-self due to ignorance in its presence. / Suffering is taught as physical-mental, and also as environmental,

1.9.s:
ādhidaivikamityuktaṃ trividhaṃ sahajaṃ punaḥ
icchāvighātātsaṃkṣobhaś cetasastadudāhṛtam //
1.9.d:
आधिदैविकमित्युक्तं त्रिविधं सहजं पुनः
इच्छाविघातात्संक्षोभश् चेतसस्तदुदाहृतम् ॥
1.9.m: and stated as supernatural; it is again threefold and innate. / Agitation of the mind arising from the thwarting of desire is declared as that [suffering].

1.9.s:
daurmanasyaṃ niroddhavyaṃ vairāgyeṇa pareṇa tu
tamasā rajasā caiva saṃspṛṣṭaṃ durmanaḥ smṛtam //
1.9.d:
दौर्मनस्यं निरोद्धव्यं वैराग्येण परेण तु
तमसा रजसा चैव संस्पृष्टं दुर्मनः स्मृतम् ॥
1.9.m: Depression must be checked by supreme detachment. / A distressed mind is considered to be one touched by tamas and rajas.

1.9.s:
tadā manasi saṃjātaṃ daurmanasyamiti smṛtam
haṭhātsvīkaraṇaṃ kṛtvā yogyāyogyavivekataḥ //
1.9.d:
तदा मनसि संजातं दौर्मनस्यमिति स्मृतम्
हठात्स्वीकरणं कृत्वा योग्यायोग्यविवेकतः ॥
1.9.m: Then, what has arisen in the mind is known as depression. / Having seized [them] by force, through discernment of the fit and the unfit,

1.9.s:
viṣayeṣu vicitreṣu jantorviṣayalolatā
antarāyā iti khyātā yogasyaite hi yoginām //
1.9.d:
विषयेषु विचित्रेषु जन्तोर्विषयलोलता
अन्तराया इति ख्याता योगस्यैते हि योगिनाम् ॥
1.9.m: a living being's craving for varied objects [is that obstacle]. / These indeed are proclaimed as obstacles to yoga for yogins.

1.9.s:
atyantotsāhayuktasya naśyanti na ca saṃśayaḥ
pranaṣṭeṣvantarāyeṣu dvijāḥ paścāddhi yoginaḥ //
1.9.d:
अत्यन्तोत्साहयुक्तस्य नश्यन्ति न च संशयः
प्रनष्टेष्वन्तरायेषु द्विजाः पश्चाद्धि योगिनः ॥
1.9.m: For one endowed with intense zeal, they perish without doubt. / When the obstacles have perished, O twice-born, afterwards for the yogin

1.9.s:
upasargāḥ pravartante sarve te 'siddhisūcakāḥ
pratibhā prathamā siddhir dvitīyā śravaṇā smṛtā //
1.9.d:
उपसर्गाः प्रवर्तन्ते सर्वे ते ऽसिद्धिसूचकाः
प्रतिभा प्रथमा सिद्धिर् द्वितीया श्रवणा स्मृता ॥
1.9.m: hindrances arise, all of which indicate imperfect attainment. / Pratibhā is the first attainment; the second is remembered as śravaṇā;

1.9.s:
vārttā tṛtīyā viprendrās turīyā ceha darśanā
āsvādā pañcamī proktā vedanā ṣaṣṭhikā smṛtā //
1.9.d:
वार्त्ता तृतीया विप्रेन्द्रास् तुरीया चेह दर्शना
आस्वादा पञ्चमी प्रोक्ता वेदना षष्ठिका स्मृता ॥
1.9.m: vārttā is the third, O best of brahmins; and here darśanā is the fourth; / āsvādā is declared the fifth, and vedanā is remembered as the sixth.

1.9.s:
svalpaṣaṭsiddhisaṃtyāgāt siddhidāḥ siddhayo muneḥ
pratibhā pratibhāvṛtiḥ pratibhāva iti sthitiḥ //
1.9.d:
स्वल्पषट्सिद्धिसंत्यागात् सिद्धिदाः सिद्धयो मुनेः
प्रतिभा प्रतिभावृतिः प्रतिभाव इति स्थितिः ॥
1.9.m: By relinquishing these six petty attainments, the sage gains attainments that grant true accomplishment. / Intuition (pratibhā) is the function of intuitive flash; its settled state is intuitive presence.

1.9.s:
buddhirvivecanā vedyaṃ budhyate buddhirucyate
sūkṣme vyavahite 'tīte viprakṛṣṭe tvanāgate //
1.9.d:
बुद्धिर्विवेचना वेद्यं बुध्यते बुद्धिरुच्यते
सूक्ष्मे व्यवहिते ऽतीते विप्रकृष्टे त्वनागते ॥
1.9.m: Intellect is discrimination; what is to be known is known, so it is called intellect. / Regarding the subtle, the concealed, the past, the distant, and the future,

1.9.s:
sarvatra sarvadā jñānaṃ pratibhānukrameṇa tu
śravaṇātsarvaśabdānām aprayatnena yoginaḥ //
1.9.d:
सर्वत्र सर्वदा ज्ञानं प्रतिभानुक्रमेण तु
श्रवणात्सर्वशब्दानाम् अप्रयत्नेन योगिनः ॥
1.9.m: knowledge everywhere and at all times comes in the course of intuition. / Hearing of all sounds without effort for the yogin,

1.9.s:
hrasvadīrghaplutādīnāṃ guhyānāṃ śravaṇādapi
sparśasyādhigamo yas tu vedanā tūpapāditā //
1.9.d:
ह्रस्वदीर्घप्लुतादीनां गुह्यानां श्रवणादपि
स्पर्शस्याधिगमो यस् तु वेदना तूपपादिता ॥
1.9.m: even the hearing of secret [sounds], short, long, prolated, and the like, [is śravaṇā]. / The perception of touch is established as vedanā;

1.9.s:
darśanāddivyarūpāṇāṃ darśanaṃ cāprayatnataḥ
saṃviddivyarase tasminn āsvādo hyaprayatnataḥ //
1.9.d:
दर्शनाद्दिव्यरूपाणां दर्शनं चाप्रयत्नतः
संविद्दिव्यरसे तस्मिन्न् आस्वादो ह्यप्रयत्नतः ॥
1.9.m: darśana is seeing divine forms without effort; / consciousness of that divine flavour without effort is āsvāda;

1.9.s:
vārttā ca divyagandhānāṃ tanmātrā buddhisaṃvidā
vindante yoginastasmād ābrahmabhuvanaṃ dvijāḥ //
1.9.d:
वार्त्ता च दिव्यगन्धानां तन्मात्रा बुद्धिसंविदा
विन्दन्ते योगिनस्तस्माद् आब्रह्मभुवनं द्विजाः ॥
1.9.m: and vārttā is the subtle element of divine smells through mental consciousness. / Therefore, yogins find [powers] up to the realm of Brahmā, O twice-born.

1.9.s:
jagatyasmin hi dehasthaṃ catuḥṣaṣṭiguṇaṃ samam
aupasargikam eteṣu guṇeṣu guṇitaṃ dvijāḥ //
1.9.d:
जगत्यस्मिन् हि देहस्थं चतुःषष्टिगुणं समम्
औपसर्गिकम् एतेषु गुणेषु गुणितं द्विजाः ॥
1.9.m: For, in this world, sixty-four qualities abiding in the body are equal; / whatever is obstacle-born is multiplied among these qualities, O twice-born.

1.9.s:
saṃtyājyaṃ sarvathā sarvam aupasargikamātmanaḥ
paiśāce pārthivaṃ cāpyaṃ rākṣasānāṃ pure dvijāḥ //
1.9.d:
संत्याज्यं सर्वथा सर्वम् औपसर्गिकमात्मनः
पैशाचे पार्थिवं चाप्यं राक्षसानां पुरे द्विजाः ॥
1.9.m: Everything of one's own that is obstacle-born must be abandoned entirely: / in the Piśāca realm, that related to earth; and that related to water in the city of the Rākṣasas, O twice-born;

1.9.s:
yākṣe tu taijasaṃ proktaṃ gāndharve śvasanātmakam
aindre vyomātmakaṃ sarvaṃ saumye caiva tu mānasam //
1.9.d:
याक्षे तु तैजसं प्रोक्तं गान्धर्वे श्वसनात्मकम्
ऐन्द्रे व्योमात्मकं सर्वं सौम्ये चैव तु मानसम् ॥
1.9.m: in the Yakṣa realm, it is stated as fiery; in the Gandharva realm, consisting of wind; / in the realm of Indra, all consists of space; and in the lunar realm, of mind;

1.9.s:
prājāpatye tvahaṅkāraṃ brāhme bodhamanuttamam
ādye cāṣṭau dvitīye ca tathā ṣoḍaśarūpakam //
1.9.d:
प्राजापत्ये त्वहङ्कारं ब्राह्मे बोधमनुत्तमम्
आद्ये चाष्टौ द्वितीये च तथा षोडशरूपकम् ॥
1.9.m: in the realm of Prajāpati, of ego; and in the realm of Brahmā, unsurpassable intellect. / In the first, there are eight forms; and in the second, sixteen;

1.9.s:
caturviṃśattṛtīye tu dvātriṃśacca caturthake
catvāriṃśat pañcame tu bhūtamātrātmakaṃ smṛtam //
1.9.d:
चतुर्विंशत्तृतीये तु द्वात्रिंशच्च चतुर्थके
चत्वारिंशत् पञ्चमे तु भूतमात्रात्मकं स्मृतम् ॥
1.9.m: twenty-four in the third; and thirty-two in the fourth; / forty in the fifth; it is considered to consist of subtle elements.

1.9.s:
gandho rasas tathā rūpaṃ śabdaḥ sparśastathaiva ca
pratyekamaṣṭadhā siddhaṃ pañcame tacchatakratoḥ //
1.9.d:
गन्धो रसस् तथा रूपं शब्दः स्पर्शस्तथैव च
प्रत्येकमष्टधा सिद्धं पञ्चमे तच्छतक्रतोः ॥
1.9.m: Smell, taste, form, sound, and likewise touch: / each is established eightfold in the fifth, that of Śatakratu (Indra).

1.9.s:
tathāṣṭacatvāriṃśac ca ṣaṭpañcāśattathaiva ca
catuḥṣaṣṭiguṇaṃ brāhmaṃ labhate dvijasattamāḥ //
1.9.d:
तथाष्टचत्वारिंशच् च षट्पञ्चाशत्तथैव च
चतुःषष्टिगुणं ब्राह्मं लभते द्विजसत्तमाः ॥
1.9.m: Likewise forty-eight, and likewise fifty-six; / sixty-four qualities in the realm of Brahmā does one obtain, O best of brahmins.

1.9.s:
aupasargikam ā brahma bhuvaneṣu parityajet
lokeṣvālokya yogena yogavitparamaṃ sukham //
1.9.d:
औपसर्गिकम् आ ब्रह्म भुवनेषु परित्यजेत्
लोकेष्वालोक्य योगेन योगवित्परमं सुखम् ॥
1.9.m: One should abandon what is obstacle-born up to the worlds of Brahmā, / having perceived through yoga the supreme bliss among the worlds, as a knower of yoga.

1.9.s:
sthūlatā hrasvatā bālyaṃ vārdhakyaṃ yauvanaṃ tathā
nānājātisvarūpaṃ ca caturbhir dehadhāraṇam //
1.9.d:
स्थूलता ह्रस्वता बाल्यं वार्धक्यं यौवनं तथा
नानाजातिस्वरूपं च चतुर्भिर् देहधारणम् ॥
1.9.m: Stoutness, shortness, childhood, old age, and youth, / manifold bodily forms, and sustaining the body by four [elements],

1.9.s:
pārthivāṃśaṃ vinā nityaṃ surabhir gandhasaṃyutaḥ
etadaṣṭaguṇaṃ proktam aiśvaryaṃ pārthivaṃ mahat //
1.9.d:
पार्थिवांशं विना नित्यं सुरभिर् गन्धसंयुतः
एतदष्टगुणं प्रोक्तम् ऐश्वर्यं पार्थिवं महत् ॥
1.9.m: ever fragrant with perfume without any earthy component— / this is declared as the great eightfold earthly sovereignty.

1.9.s:
jale nivasanaṃ yadvad bhūmyāmiva vinirgamaḥ
icchecchaktaḥ svayaṃ pātuṃ samudramapi nāturaḥ //
1.9.d:
जले निवसनं यद्वद् भूम्यामिव विनिर्गमः
इच्छेच्छक्तः स्वयं पातुं समुद्रमपि नातुरः ॥
1.9.m: Dwelling in water just like on earth, and emerging likewise; / if he wishes, he is capable of drinking even the ocean without distress;

1.9.s:
yatrecchati jagatyasmiṃs tatrāsya jaladarśanam
yadyadvastu samādāya bhoktumicchati kāmataḥ //
1.9.d:
यत्रेच्छति जगत्यस्मिंस् तत्रास्य जलदर्शनम्
यद्यद्वस्तु समादाय भोक्तुमिच्छति कामतः ॥
1.9.m: wherever in this world he wishes, there he beholds water; / whatever object he takes and wishes to consume at will,

1.9.s:
tattadrasānvitaṃ tasya trayāṇāṃ dehadhāraṇam
bhāṇḍaṃ vinātha hastena jalapiṇḍasya dhāraṇam //
1.9.d:
तत्तद्रसान्वितं तस्य त्रयाणां देहधारणम्
भाण्डं विनाथ हस्तेन जलपिण्डस्य धारणम् ॥
1.9.m: endowed with that very flavour; sustaining the body by three [elements]; / holding a sphere of water in his hand without a vessel;

1.9.s:
avraṇatvaṃ śarīrasya pārthivena samanvitam
